units.zh: 志第十三 五行一
units.en: Treatise Thirteen: The Five Elements, Part One.
units.literal: Treatise, the thirteenth: Five Elements, part one.

units.zh: 貌不恭 淫雨 服妖 雞禍 青眚 屋自壞 訛言 旱 謠 狼食人
units.en: Undignified bearing; unseasonable downpours; dress as ill omen; calamities involving fowl; greenish spectral blights; dwellings that fall without human cause; lying rumors; drought; rhymed portents; wolves that prey on men.
units.literal: Lack of dignity in demeanor; excessive rain; clothing prodigies; chicken disasters; green calamities; houses collapsing of themselves; false rumors; drought; songs and portents; wolves devouring people.

units.zh: 《五行傳》說及其占應，《漢書·五行志》錄之詳矣。
units.en: The classic exposition in the Treatise on the Five Elements, with the omens read from it and the events that answered them, was already set down at length in the Book of Han's treatise on the subject.
units.literal: The Treatise on the Five Elements sets forth the theory together with its divination and corresponding events; the "Treatise on the Five Elements" in the Book of Han recorded these in detail.

units.zh: 故泰山太守應劭、給事中董巴、散騎常侍譙周並撰建武以來災異。
units.en: Ying Shao, who had governed Taishan, the palace attendant Dong Ba, and Qiao Zhou, a regular attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, each compiled records of portents and disasters from the opening of the Jianwu reign onward.
units.literal: Therefore Ying Shao, prefect of Taishan, Dong Ba, palace attendant, and Qiao Zhou, regular attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, together compiled prodigies and anomalies since the Jianwu era.

units.zh: 今合而論之，以續《前志》云。
units.en: Here those materials are brought together and discussed in one place, extending the earlier treatise.
units.literal: Now combining and discussing them, so as to continue the former treatise.

units.zh: 《五行傳》曰：「田獵不宿，飲食不享，出入不節，奪民農時，及有姦謀，則木不曲直。」
units.en: The Treatise on the Five Elements declares: "When the ruler hunts without pause, feasts without making the proper offerings, comes and goes without measure, robs the people of their seasons for tillage, and harbors secret treachery, the virtue associated with wood fails—wood no longer 'bends and straightens' as it ought."
units.literal: The Treatise on the Five Elements says: "If one hunts without resting between outings, if one eats and drinks without offering sacrifice, if comings and goings lack moderation, if the people's farming seasons are seized from them, and if there are treacherous plots, then wood will not bend and straighten as it should."

units.zh: 謂木失其性而爲災也。
units.en: That is to say, the nature of wood is corrupted and disaster follows.
units.literal: This means that wood loses its nature and becomes a disaster.

units.zh: 又曰：「貌之不恭，是謂不肅。
units.en: It continues: "When bearing is irreverent, that is termed a failure of awe-inspiring demeanor.
units.literal: It also says: "When there is lack of dignity in outward demeanor, this is called lack of solemnity.

units.zh: 厥咎狂，厥罰恒雨，厥極惡。
units.en: The blame falls on frenzy; the chastisement is unrelenting rain; the worst outcome is thoroughgoing evil.
units.literal: Its fault is madness; its punishment is constant rain; its extreme is wickedness.

units.zh: 時則有服妖，時則有龜孽，時則有雞禍，時則有下體生上之痾，時則有青眚、青祥，惟金沴木。」
units.en: In such times appear freaks of dress, omens involving turtles, calamities among fowl, ailments that afflict the lower body yet show on the upper, bluish-green spectral visitations and greenish good-luck prodigies—metal, in the cycle of qi, is said to harm wood."
units.literal: Then there are clothing prodigies, then tortoise prodigies, then chicken disasters, then illness of the lower body appearing on the upper, then green calamities and green auspices—only metal injures wood."

units.zh: 說云：氣之相傷謂之沴。
units.en: Commentary explains that when one phase of qi wounds another, that interaction is called li—injurious encroachment.
units.literal: The explanation states: mutual injury among qi is called li (injurious interference).

units.zh: 建武元年，赤眉賊率樊崇、逢安等共立劉盆子爲天子。
units.en: In Jianwu's first year the Red Eyebrows, under Fan Chong and Feng An, enthroned the boy Liu Penzi as emperor.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, the Red Eyebrow bandits, led by Fan Chong, Feng An, and others, together set up Liu Penzi as Son of Heaven.

units.zh: 然崇等視之如小兒，百事自由，初不恤錄也。
units.en: Yet Chong and the others treated him like a small child; in a hundred affairs he had a free hand, and at first they did not bother to restrain or keep a record of him.
units.literal: Yet Chong and the others treated him like a small child; in a hundred affairs he had freedom, and at first they did not care to restrain or supervise him.

units.zh: 後正旦至，君臣欲共饗，既坐，酒食未下，羣臣更起，亂不可整。
units.en: At the New Year banquet they had barely sat down when, before a cup was poured, the courtiers were on their feet again in such confusion that no one could restore order.
units.literal: Later when New Year's Day arrived, ruler and ministers wished to feast together; they had already taken their seats, but before wine and food were served, the host of ministers rose one after another, and the disorder could not be set right.

units.zh: 時，大司農楊音案劒怒曰：「小兒戲尚不如此！」
units.en: At that time Grand Minister of Agriculture Yang Yin, grasping his sword in anger, said: "Even children's play is not like this!"
units.literal: At that time Grand Minister of Agriculture Yang Yin, grasping his sword in anger, said: "Even children's play is not like this!"

units.zh: 其後遂破壞，崇、安等皆誅死。
units.en: The regime soon fell apart, and Fan Chong, Feng An, and their fellows were put to death.
units.literal: Afterward it was destroyed and broken up; Chong, An, and the others were all executed.

units.zh: 唯音爲關内侯，以壽終。
units.en: Yang Yin alone was ennobled as a marquis within the passes and died in bed of old age.
units.literal: Only Yin became marquis within the passes and ended his life by natural death.

units.zh: 光武崩，山陽王荆哭不哀，作飛書與東海王，勸使作亂。
units.en: After Guangwu's death Prince Jing of Shanyang wept without grief; he composed a flying letter to the Prince of Donghai, urging him to rise in rebellion.
units.literal: When Guangwu died, the Prince of Shanyang, Liu Jing, wept without grief; he composed a flying letter to the Prince of Donghai, urging him to rise in rebellion.

units.zh: 明帝以荆同母弟，太后在，故隱之。
units.en: Emperor Ming hushed the affair out of respect for his mother the dowager, for Jing was his full brother.
units.literal: Mingdi, because Jing was his younger brother by the same mother and the empress dowager was still alive, therefore concealed the matter.

units.zh: 後徙王廣陵，荆遂坐復謀反自殺也。
units.en: Later, when Jing was transferred to the kingdom of Guangling, he was caught plotting rebellion a second time and took his own life.
units.literal: Later he was removed and made king of Guangling; Jing then sat guilty of again plotting rebellion and committed suicide.

units.zh: 章帝時，竇皇后兄憲以皇后甚幸於上，故人人莫不畏憲。
units.en: Under Emperor Zhang, Dou Xian—the empress's brother—terrified the whole court because his sister held the emperor's complete favor.
units.literal: In Zhangdi's time, Dou Xian, elder brother of Empress Dou, because the empress was greatly favored by the sovereign, therefore there was no one who did not fear Xian.

units.zh: 憲於是強請奪沁水長公主田，公主畏憲，與之，憲乃賤顧之。
units.en: He bullied the senior Princess of Qinshui into surrendering her estate; once she yielded out of fear, he treated her with open contempt.
units.literal: Xian thereupon forcibly requested to seize the fields of the senior princess of Qinshui; the princess feared Xian and gave them to him; Xian then looked back on her with contempt.

units.zh: 後上幸公主田，覺之，問憲，憲又上言借之。
units.en: When the emperor later rode over those same fields and learned the truth, he confronted Dou Xian, who brazenly claimed he had only borrowed the land.
units.literal: Later when the sovereign visited the princess's fields, he perceived it; he questioned Xian, and Xian again submitted a memorial saying he had borrowed them.

units.zh: 上以后故，但譴敕之，不治其罪。
units.en: For the empress's sake the emperor limited himself to a stern reprimand and brought no charges.
units.literal: The sovereign, because of the empress, only rebuked and admonished him and did not punish his crime.

units.zh: 後章帝崩，竇太后攝政，憲秉機密，忠直之臣與憲忤者，憲多害之，其後憲兄弟遂皆被誅。
units.en: After Zhangdi's death the Dou empress dowager ruled as regent while Dou Xian monopolized confidential business; anyone who stood up to him tended to disappear, until at last the whole Dou clan was wiped out.
units.literal: Later when Zhangdi died, Empress Dowager Dou held the government; Xian grasped secret affairs; of the loyal and upright ministers who opposed Xian, Xian for the most part harmed them; afterward Xian and his brothers were all executed.

units.zh: 桓帝時，梁冀秉政，兄弟貴盛自恣，好驅馳過度，至於歸家，猶馳驅入門。
units.en: Under Emperor Huan, Liang Ji dominated the government; his brothers were swaggering magnates who raced their chariots past all decency and would thunder through their own gates at a gallop.
units.literal: In Huandi's time, Liang Ji held power; his brothers were noble and flourishing and gave themselves free rein; they loved to gallop to excess, so that even when returning home they still galloped through the gate.

units.zh: 百姓號之曰「梁氏滅門驅馳」，後遂誅滅。
units.en: People took to calling their racing "the Liangs' headlong ride to clan extinction"—and in the end the prophecy was fulfilled to the letter.
units.literal: The common people called it "the Liang clan's gallop to extermination of the whole house"; afterward they were indeed executed and destroyed.

units.zh: 和帝永元十年、十三年、十四年、十五年，皆淫雨傷稼。
units.en: Four separate years of Emperor He's Yongyuan era—10, 13, 14, and 15—brought such relentless rain that the harvests rotted in the fields.
units.literal: In Emperor He's Yongyuan reign, the tenth, thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth years, in all cases excessive rain harmed the crops.

units.zh: 古今注曰：「光武建武六年九月，大雨連月，苗稼更生，鼠巢樹上。
units.en: The Ancient and Modern Notes record: "In the ninth month of Jianwu 6 under Emperor Guangwu rain fell for months; shoots regrew and rats nested in the trees.
units.literal: Ancient and Modern Notes says: "In the ninth month of Emperor Guangwu's sixth year of Jianwu, great rain lasted months; seedling crops sprouted anew and rats nested in trees.

units.zh: 十七年，雒陽暴雨，壞民廬舍，壓殺人，傷害禾稼。」
units.en: In year 17 a Luoyang storm wrecked houses, crushed people, and ruined the harvest."
units.literal: In the seventeenth year, a cloudburst in Luoyang destroyed commoners' huts, crushed people to death, and harmed grain crops."

units.zh: 安帝元初四年秋，郡國十淫雨傷稼。
units.en: In the autumn of Yuanchu 4 under Emperor An, ten provinces suffered ruinous rains.
units.literal: In the autumn of Emperor An's fourth year of Yuanchu, ten commanderies and kingdoms had excessive rain that harmed crops.

units.zh: 永寧元年，郡國三十三淫雨傷稼。
units.en: The first year of Yongning saw thirty-three commanderies and kingdoms deluged until the grain failed.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongning, thirty-three commanderies and kingdoms had excessive rain that harmed the crops.

units.zh: 建光元年，京都及郡國二十九淫雨傷稼。
units.en: Jianguang's first year brought the same affliction to the capital and twenty-nine other jurisdictions.
units.literal: In the first year of Jianguang, the capital region and twenty-nine commanderies and kingdoms had excessive rain that harmed the crops.

units.zh: 是時羌反久未平，百姓屯戍，不解愁苦。
units.en: The Qiang revolt still raged, and the people—stuck in endless garrison duty—had no respite from misery.
units.literal: At this time the Qiang rebellion had long not been pacified; the common people were garrisoned on campaign and could not be relieved of sorrow and bitterness.

units.zh: 延光元年，郡國二十七淫雨傷稼。
units.en: Yanguang's first year added twenty-seven more regions where the rains spoiled the harvest.
units.literal: In the first year of Yanguang, twenty-seven commanderies and kingdoms had excessive rain that harmed the crops.

units.zh: 二年，郡國五連雨傷稼。
units.en: The following year five commanderies suffered week after week of rain and lost their crops.
units.literal: In the second year, five commanderies and kingdoms had continuous rain that harmed the crops.

units.zh: 順帝永建四年，司隸、荆、豫、兗、冀部淫雨傷稼。
units.en: In the fourth year of Yongjian under Emperor Shun, the capital inspectorate and the Jing, Yu, Yan, and Ji macro-regions were drowned by unseasonable rains.
units.literal: In Emperor Shun's fourth year of Yongjian, the Metropolitan Province and the Jing, Yu, Yan, and Ji regions had excessive rain that harmed the crops.

units.zh: 六年，冀州淫雨傷稼。
units.en: Two years later Ji Province alone was battered by the same scourge.
units.literal: In the sixth year, Ji Province had excessive rain that harmed the crops.

units.zh: 桓帝延熹二年夏，霖雨五十餘日。
units.en: In the second summer of Emperor Huan's Yanxi era the skies opened for fifty-odd days of steady downpour.
units.literal: In Emperor Huan's second year of Yanxi, summer, there was soaking rain for more than fifty days.

units.zh: 是時，大將軍梁冀秉政，謀害上所幸鄧貴人母宣，冀又擅殺議郎邴尊。
units.en: Liang Ji was then dictator at court: he schemed against Lady Deng's mother Xuan, whom the emperor cherished, and he murdered the advisor Bing Zun without trial.
units.literal: At this time the great general Liang Ji held power; he plotted to harm Xuan, mother of the honored Lady Deng whom the sovereign favored; Ji also on his own authority killed Gentleman-advisor Bing Zun.

units.zh: 上欲誅冀，懼其持權日久，威勢強盛，恐有逆命，害及吏民，密與近臣中常侍單超等圖其方畧。
units.en: The emperor meant to destroy Liang Ji yet dreaded the general's entrenched might; he feared a violent refusal that would cost officials and commoners their lives, so he took Shan Chao and other trusted eunuchs into his confidence and worked out a plan in secret.
units.literal: The sovereign wished to execute Ji, but feared that because he had held power a long time his awesomeness and strength were great, and dreaded that there might be defiance of orders, harm reaching officials and people; he secretly with close ministers, palace attendant Shan Chao and others, plotted the strategy.

units.zh: 其年八月，冀卒伏罪誅滅。
units.en: In the eighth month of that same year Liang Ji was convicted and the entire faction extirpated.
units.literal: That year in the eighth month, Ji finally submitted to guilt and was executed and exterminated.

units.zh: 中平六年夏，霖雨八十餘日。
units.en: The sixth year of Zhongping brought eighty-some days of unbroken summer rain.
units.literal: In the sixth year of Zhongping, summer, there was soaking rain for more than eighty days.

units.zh: 是時，靈帝新棄羣臣，大行尚在梓宫，大將軍何進與佐軍校尉袁紹等共謀欲誅廢中官。
units.en: Emperor Ling had just died; his bier still stood in the palace when He Jin the general-in-chief and Yuan Shao, an assistant commandant of the army, conspired to slaughter the eunuchs and strip them of office.
units.literal: At this time Lingdi had newly abandoned the host of ministers; the grand procession was still in the catalpa coffin; the great general He Jin with assistant army commandant Yuan Shao and others together plotted wishing to execute and abolish the inner court eunuchs.

units.zh: 下文陵畢，中常侍張讓等共殺進，兵戰京都，死者數千。
units.en: Once Emperor Ling had been interred at Wenling, Zhang Rang and his fellow eunuchs cut down He Jin; Luoyang erupted in street fighting and thousands died.
units.literal: After the burial rites at Wenling were completed, palace attendants Zhang Rang and others together killed Jin; soldiers fought in the capital region; those who died were several thousand.

units.zh: 更始諸將軍過雒陽者數十辈，皆帻而衣婦人衣繡擁蕭。
units.en: Dozens of Gengshi-era generals marched through Luoyang wearing turbans over women's embroidered gowns, their hair dressed in elaborate coils.
units.literal: The various generals of Gengshi who passed through Luoyang numbered several tens of parties; all wore headcloths and dressed in women's embroidered clothing with piled-up sedge.

units.zh: 時，智者見之，以爲服之不中，身之災也，乃奔入邊郡避之。
units.en: Thoughtful observers took this perversion of dress for a personal ill omen and fled to the frontier for safety.
units.literal: At that time, when wise men saw it, they considered that clothing not hitting the mark was a disaster for the person; they then fled into border commanderies to avoid it.

units.zh: 是服妖也。
units.en: This was reckoned a "clothing prodigy" in the sense of the omen texts.
units.literal: This was a clothing prodigy.

units.zh: 其後更始遂爲赤眉所殺。
units.en: Gengshi soon fell to the Red Eyebrows and lost his life.
units.literal: Afterward Gengshi was then killed by the Red Eyebrows.

units.zh: 桓帝元嘉中，京都婦女作愁眉、啼粧、堕馬髻、折要步、齲齒笑。
units.en: During Emperor Huan's Yuanjia years the women of Luoyang took up "grieving" brows, tear-stained cosmetics, side-swept chignons styled like a tumble from a horse, a mincing walk that snapped at the waist, and smiles that bared teeth as if in pain.
units.literal: In Huandi's Yuanjia era, capital women made sorrowful brows, weeping makeup, fallen-horse chignons, broken-waist gait, and decayed-tooth smiles.

units.zh: 所謂愁眉者，細而曲折。
units.en: The "sorrowful" brow was plucked thin and drawn in nervous curves.
units.literal: What is called sorrowful brows means fine and tortuous.

units.zh: 啼粧者，薄拭目下，若啼處。
units.en: The "weeping" face was rouged only under the eyes, as though fresh from tears.
units.literal: Weeping makeup means lightly wiping beneath the eyes as if a place where one weeps.

units.zh: 堕馬髻者，作一邊。
units.en: The "fallen-from-a-horse" coiffure swept all the hair to one side.
units.literal: Fallen-horse chignon means made to one side.

units.zh: 折要步者，足不在體下。
units.en: The "broken waist" walk kept the feet from falling straight under the torso—an exaggerated sway.
units.literal: Broken-waist gait means the feet are not beneath the body.

units.zh: 齲齒笑者，若齒痛，樂不欣欣。
units.en: The "rotting-tooth" smile looked like a wince of dental pain—mirth without merriment.
units.literal: Decay-tooth smile means as if the teeth hurt; joy is not bright and glad.

units.zh: 始自大將軍梁冀家所爲，京都歙然，諸夏皆放效。
units.en: The fashion started in General Liang Ji's mansion, swept the capital overnight, and was copied through the heartland.
units.literal: It began as what was done in the household of the great general Liang Ji; the capital sucked in its breath; all the Xia lands imitated it.

units.zh: 此近服妖也。
units.en: This was reckoned a near cousin to the omen of freakish dress.
units.literal: This was near to a clothing prodigy.

units.zh: 梁冀二世上將，婚媾王室，大作威福，將危社稷。
units.en: For two generations the Liangs had held the supreme command, intermarried with the imperial clan, thrown their weight about, and brought the dynasty to the brink.
units.literal: Liang Ji for two generations was chief general; he married into the royal house and greatly made awesomeness and blessings, about to endanger the altars of soil and grain.

units.zh: 天誡若曰：「兵馬將往收捕，婦女憂愁，踧眉啼泣，吏卒掣頓，折其要脊，令髻傾邪，雖強語笑，无復氣味也。」
units.en: Heaven seemed to warn: "Troops are coming to drag families away—women will weep and cringe, guards will wrench their backs and snap their spines, their hair will hang askew, and any laughter they manage will be hollow."
units.literal: Heaven's warning was as if saying: "When horses and foot-soldiers are about to go to seize and capture, women are anxious and sorrowful, knitting their brows and weeping; clerks and soldiers drag and halt them, break their waist and spine, make their chignons lean awry; though they force speech and laughter, there is no more breath or flavor."

units.zh: 到延熹二年，舉宗誅夷。
units.en: In the second Yanxi year the entire Liang clan was extirpated.
units.literal: When it reached the second year of Yanxi, the whole clan was executed and exterminated.

units.zh: 延熹中，梁冀誅后，京都帻颜短耳長，短上長下。
units.en: After Liang Ji's fall, during the Yanxi years, Luoyang took to turbans cut short across the crown with long flaps at the ears—the upper line abrupt, the lower line drawn out.
units.literal: In the Yanxi era, after Liang Ji was executed, in the capital the headcloth's face was short and the ears long, short above and long below.

units.zh: 時中常侍單超、左悺、徐璜、具瑗、唐衡在帝左右，縱其姦慝。
units.en: Shan Chao, Zuo Guan, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, and Tang Heng—the eunuch quintet at the emperor's elbow—ran wild with corruption.
units.literal: At that time palace attendants Shan Chao, Zuo Guan, Xu Huang, Ju Yuan, and Tang Heng were at the emperor's side and gave free rein to their treacherous wickedness.

units.zh: 海内愠曰：一將軍死，五將軍出。
units.en: A bitter proverb ran through the realm: "One general-in-chief falls—five spring up to replace him."
units.literal: Within the seas people resentfully said: one general died, five generals came forth.

units.zh: 家有數侯，子弟列布州郡，宾客杂袭腾翥，上短下長，與梁冀同占。
units.en: Each household boasted multiple marquises, their sons planted in every province, their clients flocking like birds on the wing; the fashion—short above, long below—mirrored the omen once read from Liang Ji's excess.
units.literal: Families had several marquises; sons and younger brothers were spread through provinces and commanderies; guests and retainers mixed and thronged, soaring upward; short above and long below, with the same divination as Liang Ji.

units.zh: 到其八年，桓帝因日蚀之變，乃拜故司徒韩寅爲司隸校尉，以次誅鉏，京都正清。
units.en: In the eighth year of that reign Emperor Huan seized on a solar eclipse as his cue, named the former Minister of Education Han Yin metropolitan commandant, and purged the eunuch faction step by step until Luoyang was clean again.
units.literal: When it reached its eighth year, Huandi because of the change of a solar eclipse then appointed former minister of education Han Yin as metropolitan commandant, and in order executed and extirpated them; the capital region was set right and cleared.

units.zh: 延熹中，京都長者皆著木屐；
units.en: During Yanxi the respectable men of Luoyang went about in wooden clogs;
units.literal: In the Yanxi era, elders of the capital all wore wooden clogs;

units.zh: 婦女始嫁，至作漆画五采爲系。
units.en: brides began tying their hair with lacquered ribbons painted in five colors.
units.literal: women beginning marriage even made lacquer-painted five-colors as ties.

units.zh: 此服妖也。
units.en: Another sign in the category of freakish dress.
units.literal: This was a clothing prodigy.

units.zh: 到九年，党事始发，傳黄門北寺，临時惶惑，不能信天任命，多有逃走不就考者，九族拘繫，及所過歷，長少婦女皆被桎梏，應木屐之象也。
units.en: In the ninth year the great proscription began; suspects were hustled into the eunuchs' North Prison. Panic spread—men no longer trusted providence, many bolted rather than face interrogation, whole clans were shackled, and wherever the dragnet reached, women young and old were marched off in cangues and leg-irons, the very picture the wooden clogs had foretold.
units.literal: When it reached the ninth year, the faction affair first broke out; it was transmitted to the Northern Office of the Yellow Gates; facing the moment, people were anxious and confused, unable to trust Heaven and accept fate; many there were who fled and did not submit to examination; nine kin were bound and tied; and wherever they passed, old and young women all wore fetters and cangues, corresponding to the image of wooden clogs.

units.zh: 靈帝建寧中，京都長者皆以苇方笥爲粧具，下士尽然。
units.en: Under Emperor Ling, during Jianning, the capital's leading families kept their cosmetics in square reed boxes—and soon every petty clerk aped the style.
units.literal: In Lingdi's Jianning era, elders of the capital all used reed square cases as toilet articles; lower gentlemen all did likewise.

units.zh: 時有識者窃言：苇方笥，郡國讞箧也；
units.en: Wits whispered that those reed cases were the very "appeal caskets" in which provinces filed criminal memorials;
units.literal: At that time someone with insight secretly said: reed square cases are the appeal boxes of commanderies and kingdoms;

units.zh: 今珍用之，此天下人皆當有罪讞於理官也。
units.en: to prize them for rouge and powder meant the whole empire would soon stand convicted before the law.
units.literal: now they are treasured and used; this means everyone under Heaven ought to have crimes appealed to the judge officials.

units.zh: 到光和三年癸丑赦令詔書，吏民依黨禁錮者赦除之，有不見文，他以類比疑者谳。
units.en: In the third year of Guanghe, on the guichou day, an edict of general amnesty lifted the faction ban—where the wording was unclear, doubtful cases were sent up for the court to decide by analogy.
units.literal: When it reached the third year of Guanghe, guichou, the amnesty-order edict: officials and people who according to the faction proscription had been proscribed were pardoned and removed; where the text was not seen, other doubtful cases by analogy were appealed for decision.

units.zh: 於是諸有黨郡皆讞廷尉，人名悉入方笥中。
units.en: Every county with a "faction" list forwarded its dossiers to the commandant of justice, and the accused were filed away—names and all—in those square reed boxes.
units.literal: Thereupon all commanderies that had faction cases all appealed to the commandant of justice; people's names all went into square cases.

units.zh: 靈帝好胡服、胡帳、胡牀、胡坐、胡飯、胡空侯、胡笛、胡舞，京都貴戚皆竞爲之。
units.en: Emperor Ling doted on frontier dress, frontier tents, folding chairs, cross-legged sitting, frontier dishes, barbarian lutes and pipes, and barbarian dance—and the great families of Luoyang rushed to outdo one another.
units.literal: Lingdi loved Hu clothing, Hu tents, Hu couches, Hu sitting, Hu food, Hu konghou, Hu flutes, Hu dances; capital nobles and kin all vied to do it.

units.zh: 此服妖也。
units.en: Another omen-class freak of dress.
units.literal: This was a clothing prodigy.

units.zh: 其後董卓多擁胡兵，填塞街衢，虏掠宫掖，发掘園陵。
units.en: Then Dong Zhuo flooded the capital with steppe troops, choked the avenues, looted the inner palaces, and broke open imperial tombs.
units.literal: Afterward Dong Zhuo for the most part gathered Hu troops, filled and blocked streets and lanes, plundered the palace apartments, and dug up park tombs.

units.zh: 靈帝於宫中西園駕四白驢，躬自操轡，驅馳周旋，以爲大樂。
units.en: In the Western Garden inside the palace Emperor Ling hitched four white donkeys, seized the reins himself, and raced in circles for sport.
units.literal: Lingdi in the palace at the Western Garden drove four white donkeys, personally grasped the reins, galloped round and about, and took it as great pleasure.

units.zh: 於是公卿貴戚转相放效，至乘辎軿以爲騎從，互相侵奪，贾與馬齊。
units.en: High ministers and imperial in-laws copied the fad until they used light wagons as outriders in their escorts, jostling one another on the road until a donkey cost as much as a horse.
units.literal: Thereupon dukes and ministers and noble kin in turn imitated one another, to the point of riding covered wagons as mounted attendants, mutually encroaching and seizing; the price matched that of horses.

units.zh: 案《易》曰：「時乘六龍以御天。」
units.en: The Book of Changes says of the sage ruler that he "rides the six dragons to traverse Heaven."
units.literal: Examining the Changes, it says: "In due season mount the six dragons to drive Heaven."

units.zh: 行天者莫若龍，行地者莫若馬。
units.en: Nothing matches the dragon for motion above, nothing the horse for motion below.
units.literal: For what travels Heaven nothing is like the dragon; for what travels Earth nothing is like the horse.

units.zh: 《詩》云：「四牡騤騤，載是常服。」
units.en: The Classic of Poetry praises the team: "Four tall stallions in full battle harness."
units.literal: The Odes says: "The four stallions are stately; they bear the regular harness."

units.zh: 「檀車煌煌，四牡彭彭。」
units.en: Elsewhere it sings of "the gleaming sandalwood car and four powerful steeds."
units.literal: "The sandalwood carriage gleams; the four stallions are vigorous."

units.zh: 夫驢乃服重致遠，上下山谷，野人之所用耳，何有帝王君子而驂服之乎！
units.en: The donkey is a beast of burden for hill folk—how could Son of Heaven or a gentleman take it for a chariot team!
units.literal: Now the donkey is for bearing heavy loads and going far, ascending and descending mountains and valleys—what the wild people use; how can there be emperors and kings and gentlemen who pair and drive them!

units.zh: 迟鈍之畜，而今貴之。
units.en: A dull, plodding creature—yet the court now prizes it.
units.literal: A slow and dull animal, yet now it is honored.

units.zh: 天意若曰：國且大亂，賢愚倒植，凡執政者皆如驢也。
units.en: Heaven's message read: "The realm will soon convulse; wise and foolish will trade places, and every man at the helm will be a donkey."
units.literal: Heaven's intent was as if saying: the state is about to be greatly disordered; worthy and foolish are inverted; all who hold power are like donkeys.

units.zh: 其後董卓陵虐王室，多援邊人以充本朝，胡夷異种，跨蹈中國。
units.en: Dong Zhuo then rode roughshod over the dynasty, drafting frontier peoples into the capital until foreign tribes overran the heartland.
units.literal: Afterward Dong Zhuo cruelly abused the royal house; he largely drew in border people to fill this court; Hu and Yi of alien stocks trampled the central states.

units.zh: 熹平中，省内冠狗带綬，以爲笑樂。
units.en: During Xiping the inner palace staged mock investitures—dogs in official caps and ribboned seals—for amusement.
units.literal: In the Xiping era, within the palace they capped dogs and belted seals of office, taking it as laughter and pleasure.

units.zh: 有一狗突出，走入司徒府門，或見之者，莫不惊怪。
units.en: One dog broke loose and dashed into the gate of the Minister of Education—every witness was struck with dread.
units.literal: There was one dog that burst out and ran into the gate of the minister of education's office; those who saw it were all startled and wondered.

units.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「君不正，臣欲篡，厥妖狗冠出。」
units.en: Jing Fang's treatise warns: "When the ruler strays from the Way and ministers plot usurpation, Heaven sends the prodigy of a dog in an official's cap."
units.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the lord is not correct, ministers wish to usurp; its prodigy is a capped dog appearing."

units.zh: 后靈帝寵用便嬖子弟，永樂宾客、鸿都羣小，傳相汲引，公卿牧守，比肩是也。
units.en: Emperor Ling went on to shower favor on his minions' sons, the hangers-on at Yongle, the riffraff of the Hongdu Academy—men who pulled one another up until every minister and provincial governor seemed cut from the same cloth.
units.literal: Later Lingdi favored and employed the sons and younger brothers of his intimates, guests of Yongle, the petty crowd of Hongdu; they transmitted and drew one another up; dukes, ministers, shepherds, and guards—shoulder to shoulder were such.

units.zh: 又遣御史於西邸卖官，關内侯顧五百萬者，赐與金紫；
units.en: He set up a market for ranks at the Western Lodge: five million cash bought a marquisate within the passes and the gold seal with purple ribbon;
units.literal: He also sent censors to the Western Lodge to sell offices; for one who looked to a marquis within the passes at five million, he was granted gold and purple;

units.zh: 詣闕上書占令長，随县好醜，豐約有賈。
units.en: Anyone could walk to the palace gate, bid for a magistracy, and pay a sliding scale—fat fees for rich counties, lean ones for poor.
units.literal: Those who went to the palace gate and submitted memorials to secure magistrates, following whether the county was good or ugly, had abundance or restraint with a price.

units.zh: 強者貪如豺虎，弱者畧不類物，實狗而冠者也。
units.en: The bold ones devoured like wolves; the timid ones scarcely looked human—they were dogs in caps, nothing more.
units.literal: The strong were greedy as jackals and tigers; the weak were in outline not like creatures—truly dogs wearing caps.

units.zh: 司徒，古之丞相，壹统國政。
units.en: The Minister of Education was once the chancellor—the officer who unified the administration of the realm.
units.literal: The minister of education is the ancient chancellor; he alone unifies state government.

units.zh: 天戒若曰：宰相多非其人，尸祿素餐，莫能据正持重，阿意曲從。
units.en: Heaven seemed to warn: "Too many chief ministers are the wrong men—drawing pay for empty seats, unable to stand firm, always trimming to the ruler's whim."
units.literal: Heaven's warning was as if saying: the ministers are mostly not the right men; they hold salary with empty white eating; none can grasp what is correct and hold weight; they flatter intent and bend in compliance.

units.zh: 今在位者皆如狗也，故狗走入其門。
units.en: The men in power were hounds in caps—which is why Heaven sent a dog through the minister's gate.
units.literal: Now those in office are all like dogs; therefore the dog ran into their gate.

units.zh: 靈帝數游戲於西園中，令後宫采女爲客舍主人，身爲商賈服。
units.en: Emperor Ling often staged bawdy play in the Western Garden, dressing palace ladies as innkeepers while he himself put on the garb of a peddler.
units.literal: Lingdi repeatedly played games in the Western Garden; he ordered rear-palace selected women to be innkeepers; he himself wore merchant-trader clothing.

units.zh: 行至舍，采女下酒食，因共飲食以爲戲樂。
units.en: He would "arrive" at the mock inn; the women served wine and food, and all feasted together for sport.
units.literal: When he walked and reached the inn, the selected women set out wine and food; thereupon they together drank and ate, taking it as playful pleasure.

units.zh: 此服妖也。
units.en: Another omen in the category of perverted dress.
units.literal: This was a clothing prodigy.

units.zh: 其後天下大亂。
units.en: The empire then slid into chaos.
units.literal: Afterward all under Heaven was greatly disordered.

units.zh: 風俗通曰：「時京師賓〈女昬〉嘉會，皆作魁〈木壘〉，酒酣之後，續以挽歌。」
units.en: The Fengsu Tong records: "At capital wedding banquets guests built funeral towers; when cups ran deep they sang dirges."
units.literal: Fengsu Tong says: "At that time at capital wedding feasts people all made kui wooden towers; after wine was deep they continued with funeral dirges."

units.zh: 魁〈木壘〉，喪家之樂。
units.en: Those towers were funeral pomp.
units.literal: Kui wooden towers are music of mourning households.

units.zh: 挽歌，執紼相偶和之者。
units.en: Dirges were sung while mourners pulled the coffin ropes together.
units.literal: Funeral dirges are those who hold mourning cords and chant antiphonally.

units.zh: 天戒若曰：國家當急殄悴，諸貴樂皆死亡也。
units.en: Heaven warned: the dynasty would perish swiftly and noble revelry would end in death.
units.literal: Heaven's warning was as if saying: the state is about to be swiftly extinguished; all the nobles' pleasures are death.

units.zh: 自靈帝崩後，京師壞滅，戶有兼屍，蟲而相食，魁〈木壘〉、挽歌，斯之效乎？
units.en: After Ling's death Luoyang collapsed with corpses heaped in every house—had not the wedding dirges foretold it?
units.literal: From after Emperor Ling's death the capital was ruined and destroyed; households had piled corpses, worms devouring one another—kui towers and funeral dirges, was this not their effect?

units.zh: 獻帝建安中，男子之衣，好爲長躬而下甚短，女子好爲長裙而上甚短。
units.en: In the Jian'an years of Emperor Xian, men wore jackets that hung long on the torso but ended abruptly at the waist, while women favored long skirts paired with bodices cut scandalously short.
units.literal: In Xiandi's Jian'an era, men's clothing favored making the upper body long while below was very short; women favored making long skirts while above was very short.

units.zh: 時益州從事莫嗣以爲服妖，是陽无下而陰无上也，天下未欲平也。
units.en: Mo Si, an aide in Yi Province, read the new fashions as an ill omen: the masculine had lost its footing, the feminine its summit—the realm was not ready to rest.
units.literal: At the time the Yizhou clerk Mo Si took it to be a clothing prodigy: this was yang having nothing below and yin having nothing above; all under Heaven did not yet desire peace.

units.zh: 后還，遂大亂。
units.en: Later he returned, and thereupon there was great disorder.
units.literal: Later he returned, and thereupon there was great disorder.

units.zh: 袁山松〔書〕曰：「禪位於魏。」
units.en: Yuan Shansong's Book records: "The throne was yielded to Wei."
units.literal: Yuan Shansong's Book says: "The abdication was transferred to Wei."

units.zh: 靈帝光和元年，南宫侍中寺雌雞欲化雄，一身毛皆似雄，但頭冠尚未變。
units.en: In Guanghe 1, at the Southern Palace's Palace Attendants' Office a hen began turning into a rooster—every feather looked male, yet the comb had not changed.
units.literal: In Emperor Ling's first year of Guanghe, at the Palace Attendants' Office in the Southern Palace a hen wished to transform into a cock; its whole body's feathers all resembled a cock's, but the head crest had not yet changed.

units.zh: 诏以問議郎蔡邕。
units.en: The court asked Cai Yong, a gentleman consultant.
units.literal: An edict asked the gentleman consultant Cai Yong.

units.zh: 邕对曰：「貌之不恭，則有雞禍。
units.en: Yong answered: "Irreverent bearing brings calamities among fowl.
units.literal: Yong replied: "When demeanor lacks dignity, there are chicken disasters.

units.zh: 宣帝黄龍元年，未央宫雌雞化爲雄，不鸣无距。
units.en: In Huanglong 1 of Emperor Xuan, a Weiyang Palace hen became a rooster that neither crowed nor grew spurs.
units.literal: In Emperor Xuan's first year of Huanglong, at Weiyang Palace a hen transformed into a cock, neither crowing nor having spurs.

units.zh: 是岁元帝初即位，立王皇后。
units.en: That year the newly enthroned Emperor Yuan made Lady Wang empress.
units.literal: That year Emperor Yuan first took the throne and installed Empress Wang.

units.zh: 至初元元年，丞相史家雌雞化爲雄，冠距鸣將。
units.en: By Chuyuan 1 a hen at a chancellor's clerk's home had become a crowing rooster with comb and spurs.
units.literal: By the first year of Chuyuan, at the chief minister's clerk's house a hen transformed into a cock, with crest, spurs, and about to crow.

units.zh: 是岁后父禁爲陽平侯，女立爲皇后。
units.en: Soon after, the empress's father Wang Jin was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangping and his daughter was crowned.
units.literal: After that year the empress's father Wang Jin became marquis of Yangping; the daughter was installed as empress.

units.zh: 至哀帝晏駕，后攝政，王莽以后兄子爲大司馬，由是爲亂。
units.en: When Emperor Ai died, the empress held the regency; Wang Mang, the empress's elder brother's son, became grand marshal—and chaos followed.
units.literal: When Emperor Ai died, the empress held regency; Wang Mang made the empress's elder brother's son grand marshal—thereby came disorder.

units.zh: 臣窃推之：頭，元首，人君之象。
units.en: I read the omen thus: the head is the sovereign's image.
units.literal: Your servant privately infers: the head is the chief member, the image of the ruler.

units.zh: 今雞一身已變，未至於頭，而上知之，是將有其事而不遂成之象也。
units.en: The bird's body had changed but not its head, yet Heaven had already warned the throne—an omen of crisis not yet complete.
units.literal: Now the chicken's whole body has changed but not yet reached the head, yet the sovereign knows it—this is the image of something about to happen but not yet fully accomplished.

units.zh: 若應之不精，政无所改，頭冠或成，爲患兹大。」
units.en: If the court ignored the warning and reformed nothing, the comb might finish forming—and the disaster would be worse."
units.literal: If the response is not precise and government changes nothing, the head crest may complete itself and the harm will be all the greater."

units.zh: 是后張角作亂称黄巾，遂破壞。
units.en: Soon Zhang Jiao raised the Yellow Turban revolt and the realm was torn apart.
units.literal: After this Zhang Jiao rebelled, calling himself the Yellow Turbans, and destruction followed.

units.zh: 四方疲於赋役，多叛者。
units.en: Taxes and labor broke the provinces; rebellion spread.
units.literal: The four quarters were exhausted by levies and corvée; many rebelled.

units.zh: 上不改政，遂至天下大亂。
units.en: The emperor changed nothing—and the empire slid into total chaos.
units.literal: The sovereign did not reform government, and all under Heaven reached great disorder.

units.zh: 桓帝永興二年四月丙午，光祿勋吏舍壁下夜有青氣，視之，得玉鈎、玦各一。
units.en: On a bingwu day in the fourth month of Yongxing 2, a greenish glow appeared at night under the eunuch finance office; when clerks dug there they found a carved jade belt hook and a broken ring.
units.literal: In Huandi's second year of Yongxing, fourth month, day bingwu, beneath the wall of the clerks' quarters of the chamberlain for the palace revenues, at night there was greenish vapor; looking at it, they obtained one jade hook and one jade ring apiece.

units.zh: 鈎長七寸二分，玦周五寸四分，身中皆雕鏤。
units.en: The hook measured seven cun two fen; the ring's girth was five cun four fen; both pieces were richly engraved.
units.literal: The hook was seven cun and two fen in length; the ring's circumference was five cun and four fen; their bodies were all carved openwork.

units.zh: 此青祥也，玉，金類也。
units.en: Green jade prodigies belong to the wood-metal nexus—jade itself counts as a metal-like substance in the scheme.
units.literal: This was a green auspice; jade is of the class of metal.

units.zh: 七寸二分，商數也。
units.en: Seven cun two fen matches the "shang" tone in the pitch-pipe numerology.
units.literal: Seven cun two fen is the shang pitch number.

units.zh: 五寸四分，徵數也。
units.en: Five cun four fen answers to the "zhi" pipe.
units.literal: Five cun four fen is the zhi pitch number.

units.zh: 商爲臣，徵爲事，盖爲人臣引决事者不肅，將有禍也。
units.en: Because "shang" codes for ministers and "zhi" for public business, the omen pointed to high officials who shaped policy without gravity—disaster would follow.
units.literal: Shang stands for ministers, zhi for affairs: it means that ministers who lead in deciding affairs are not solemn; there will be disaster.

units.zh: 是時梁冀秉政專恣，后四岁，梁氏誅滅也。
units.en: Liang Ji was then absolute master of the court; four years later his whole clan was extirpated.
units.literal: At that time Liang Ji held power and was wantonly autocratic; after four years the Liang clan was executed and destroyed.

units.zh: 延熹五年，太学門无故自壞。
units.en: In Yanxi 5 the main gate of the Imperial Academy fell in though no one had touched it.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Yanxi, the gate of the Imperial Academy for no reason collapsed of itself.

units.zh: 襄楷以爲太学前疑所居，其門自壞，文德將喪，教化廢也。
units.en: Xiang Kai argued that the Imperial Academy was where the Qianyi counselors had resided; when its gate gave way of its own accord, it foretold the collapse of moral culture and the abandonment of education.
units.literal: Xiang Kai considered that the Imperial Academy was where the former doubtful resided; its gate collapsed of itself: civil virtue was about to be lost, instruction and transformation were abandoned.

units.zh: 是後天下遂至喪亂。
units.en: The empire soon sank into anarchy.
units.literal: After this all under Heaven thereupon reached ruin and disorder.

units.zh: 永康元年十月壬戌，南宫平城門内屋自壞。
units.en: On a renxu day in the tenth month of Yongkang 1, structures inside Luoyang's Pingcheng Gate in the Southern Palace fell without warning.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongkang, tenth month, day renxu, buildings inside the Pingcheng Gate of the Southern Palace collapsed of themselves.

units.zh: 金沴木，木動也。
units.en: Metal was encroaching on wood—the element of timber shook.
units.literal: Metal injures wood; wood moved.

units.zh: 其十二月，宫車晏駕。
units.en: In the twelfth month the emperor died—the euphemism "the palace carriage tarried."
units.literal: That twelfth month, the palace carriage delayed its departure (the emperor died).

units.zh: 靈帝光和元年，南宫平城門内屋、武庫屋及外東垣屋前後頓壞。
units.en: In Guanghe 1 structures inside Luoyang's Pingcheng Gate, the armory, and the eastern outer wall all collapsed at once.
units.literal: In Emperor Ling's first year of Guanghe, buildings inside Pingcheng Gate of the Southern Palace, the armory buildings, and the outer eastern wall buildings before and behind suddenly collapsed.

units.zh: 蔡邕对曰：「平城門，正陽之門，與宫連，郊祀法駕所由從出，門之最尊者也。
units.en: Cai Yong explained: "Pingcheng Gate is the chief yang gate linked to the palace—the ceremonial exit for suburban rites and the noblest gate of all.
units.literal: Cai Yong replied: "Pingcheng Gate is the gate of true yang, connected with the palace, the route by which the suburban-sacrifice imperial equipage goes forth—it is the most honored of gates.

units.zh: 武庫，禁兵所藏。
units.en: The armory holds the imperial arsenal.
units.literal: The armory is where forbidden troops are stored.

units.zh: 東桓，庫之外障。
units.en: The eastern rampart shields the depot.
units.literal: The eastern wall is the outer barrier of the storehouse.

units.zh: 《易傳》曰：'小人在位，上下咸悖，厥妖城門内崩。
units.en: The Changes commentary warns: "When petty men rule and hierarchy collapses, gates fall inward."
units.literal: The Commentary on the Changes says: "Petty men hold office; above and below alike rebel; its prodigy is collapse within the city gate."

units.zh: '《潜潭巴》曰：'宫瓦自堕，諸侯強陵主。
units.en: 'The Secret Depths of the Ba adds: "Roof tiles drop on their own when lords bully their sovereign."'
units.literal: 'The Secret Depths of the Ba says: "Palace tiles fall of themselves; feudal lords forcibly encroach on the lord."'

units.zh: '此皆小人顯位亂法之咎也。」
units.en: 'All are punishments for upstart villains who wreck the laws.'
units.literal: 'All these are blames for petty men in conspicuous posts who disorder the law.'

units.zh: 其后黄巾賊先起東方，庫兵大動。
units.en: The Yellow Turbans then erupted in the east and the armory shook.
units.literal: After this the Yellow Turban bandits first rose in the east; armory weapons moved greatly.

units.zh: 皇后同父兄何進爲大將軍，同母弟苗爲車騎將軍，兄弟並貴盛，皆统兵在京都。
units.en: Empress He's half-brother He Jin became grand general and her younger brother He Miao general of chariots and cavalry—both swaggered through the capital at the head of armies.
units.literal: The empress's elder brother by the same father He Jin became grand general; her younger brother by the same mother Miao became general of chariots and cavalry; the brothers together were noble and flourishing, all commanding troops in the capital.

units.zh: 其后進欲誅廢中官，爲中常侍張讓、段珪等所殺，兵戰宫中闕下，更相誅滅，天下兵大起。
units.en: When He Jin moved against the eunuchs, Zhang Rang and Duan Gui killed him; battle raged at the palace gates, factions slaughtered one another, and war engulfed the empire.
units.literal: Afterward Jin wished to execute and abolish the palace attendants; he was killed by regular palace attendants Zhang Rang, Duan Gui, and others; troops fought beneath the palace gate-towers, mutually executing and destroying one another, and armies rose throughout the realm.

units.zh: 三年二月，公府驻駕庑自壞，南北三十餘間。
units.en: In the third year, second month, the colonnade where ministers waited on the imperial progress collapsed—over thirty bays along the north-south range.
units.literal: In the third year, second month, the portico where the public offices halted the imperial carriage collapsed of itself, more than thirty bays north and south.

units.zh: 中平一年二月癸亥，廣陽城門外上屋自壞也。
units.en: On a guihai day in the second month of Zhongping 1, the upper structures outside Luoyang's Guangyang Gate crumbled on their own.
units.literal: In the first year of Zhongping, second month, day guihai, the upper buildings outside the Guangyang city gate collapsed of themselves.

units.zh: 獻帝初平二年三月，長安宣平城門外屋无故自壞。
units.en: In the third month of Chuping 2, under Emperor Xian, the buildings outside Chang'an's Xuanping Gate fell in though no storm had struck.
units.literal: In Xiandi's second year of Chuping, third month, buildings outside Chang'an's Xuanping city gate for no reason collapsed of themselves.

units.zh: 至三年夏，司徒王允使中郎將吕布殺太师董卓，夷三族。
units.en: In the summer of the third year Minister Wang Yun sent Lü Bu to cut down Dong Zhuo the grand preceptor and wipe out three generations of his kin.
units.literal: By the third year, summer, Minister of Education Wang Yun had leader of gentlemen cadets Lü Bu kill grand preceptor Dong Zhuo and exterminate three clans.

units.zh: 《五行傳》曰：「好攻戰，轻百姓，饰城郭，侵邊境，則金不從革。」
units.en: The Treatise on the Five Elements warns that when rulers delight in war, despise the people, gild their ramparts, and raid the frontiers, the virtue of metal fails—it no longer "yields and changes" as it should.
units.literal: The Treatise on the Five Elements says: "If one loves attacking and warfare, treats the common people lightly, adorns city walls, and encroaches on the borderlands, then metal will not follow and transform."

units.zh: 謂金失其性而爲災也。
units.en: That is, the nature of metal is corrupted and calamity follows.
units.literal: This means that metal loses its nature and becomes a disaster.

units.zh: 又曰：「言之不從，是謂不乂。
units.en: It adds: "When counsel goes unheeded, that is termed a breakdown of good government.
units.literal: It also says: "When speech does not obey, this is called lack of order (bu yi).

units.zh: 厥咎僭，厥罰恒陽，厥極憂。
units.en: The fault is overreaching; the scourge is relentless drought; the bitter end is widespread grief.
units.literal: Its fault is usurpation; its punishment is constant yang (drought); its extreme is sorrow.

units.zh: 時則有詩妖，時則有介虫之孽，時則有犬禍，時則有口舌之痾，時則有白眚、白祥、惟木沴金。」
units.en: Such ages bring rhymed portents, plagues among armored insects, canine omens, ailments of speech, pallid spectral blights—and in the cycle of qi, wood is said to harm metal."
units.literal: Then there are song prodigies, then shelled-insect prodigies, then dog disasters, then illness of mouth and tongue, then white calamities and white auspices—only wood injures metal."

units.zh: 介虫，劉歆傳以爲毛虫。
units.en: Commentators following Liu Xin class the "shelled" pests with hairy vermin omens.
units.literal: Shelled insects—in Liu Xin's transmission they are taken to be hairy creatures.

units.zh: 乂，治也。
units.en: Here yi means orderly rule.
units.literal: Yi means to govern.

units.zh: 安帝永初元年十一月，民讹言相惊，司隸、並、冀州民人流移。
units.en: In the eleventh month of Yongchu 1 wild rumors threw the people into panic; refugees streamed from the capital region, Bing, and Ji.
units.literal: In Emperor An's first year of Yongchu, eleventh month, the people with false words alarmed one another; the people of the Metropolitan Province, Bing, and Ji flowed away in migration.

units.zh: 時，鄧太皇專政。
units.en: Empress Dowager Deng was then regent in all but name.
units.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Deng held sole power.

units.zh: 婦人以順爲道，故《禮》「夫死從子」之命。
units.en: Women take compliance as their way; therefore the Rites have the command "when the husband dies, follow the son."
units.literal: Women take compliance as their way; therefore the Rites have the command "when the husband dies, follow the son."

units.zh: 今專主事，此不從而僭也。
units.en: To monopolize state business was neither "following" a man nor staying within a woman's sphere—it was usurpation.
units.literal: Now she solely presides over affairs; this is not obeying but usurping.

units.zh: 古今注曰：「章帝建初五年，東海、魯國、東平、山陽、濟陰、陳留民訛言相驚有賊，捕至京師，民皆入城也。」
units.en: The Ancient and Modern Notes record: "In Jianchu 5 of Emperor Zhang, six eastern provinces panicked over false reports of bandits; suspects were dragged to the capital and townsfolk fled behind city walls."
units.literal: Ancient and Modern Notes say: "In the fifth year of Emperor Zhang's Jianchu, the people of Donghai, Lu, Dongping, Shanyang, Jiyin, and Chenliu alarmed one another with false rumors of bandits; they were seized and brought to the capital, and the people all entered the cities."

units.zh: 世祖古今注曰：「建武三年七月，雒陽大旱，帝至南郊求雨，即日雨。」
units.en: The Founder's Ancient and Modern Notes record: "In the seventh month of Jianwu 3 Luoyang baked; the emperor prayed at the southern altar and rain came the same day."
units.literal: The Ancient and Modern Notes of the Founder say: "In the seventh month of the third year of Jianwu Luoyang had great drought; the emperor went to the southern suburb to pray for rain, and rain fell that day."

units.zh: 世祖建武五年夏，旱。
units.en: A drought struck in the summer of Emperor Guangwu's fifth Jianwu year.
units.literal: In Shizu's fifth year of Jianwu, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 《京房傳》曰：「欲德不用，兹謂張，厥災荒，其旱陰雲不雨，變而赤，因四陰。
units.en: Jing Fang lists omens of drought: "when virtue is spurned, Heaven stretches the land into waste; clouds gather but yield no rain, then flush an ominous red as yin forces encroach.
units.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise says: "When desired virtue is not used, this is called stretching; its disaster is wasteland; its drought—yin clouds do not rain, they change and become red, following the four yin.

units.zh: 眾出過時，兹謂廣，其旱不生。
units.en: Armies kept in the field too long "spread" exhaustion; the fields then refuse every shoot.
units.literal: When hosts go out beyond the season, this is called broadening; its drought—nothing grows.

units.zh: 上下皆蔽，兹謂隔，其旱天赤三月，時有雹殺飛禽。
units.en: When ruler and minister deceive each other, Heaven "blocks" the rain—the heavens burn red for months and hailstones cut down birds in flight.
units.literal: When above and below are both obscured, this is called blocking; its drought—the sky is red three months; at times hail kills flying birds.

units.zh: 上缘求妃，兹謂僭，其旱三月大温亡云。
units.en: A ruler who chases women beyond measure commits usurpation against Heaven; the land then swelters for three cloudless months.
units.literal: When the sovereign on account seeks concubines, this is called usurpation; its drought—three months of great warmth without clouds.

units.zh: 君高臺府，兹謂犯，陰侵陽，其旱萬物根死，有火災。
units.en: Towering palaces offend the balance of yin and yang; drought kills every root, and fires follow.
units.literal: When the lord raises high terraces and mansions, this is called violation; yin encroaches on yang; its drought—the roots of the myriad things die; there are fire disasters.

units.zh: 庶位逾節，兹謂僭，其旱泽物枯，爲火所傷。」
units.en: When petty officials overstep their rank, usurpation dries the wetlands and scorches what should be moist."
units.literal: When common offices exceed their measure, this is called usurpation; its drought—marsh things wither and are harmed by fire."

units.zh: 是時，天下僭逆者未尽誅，軍多過時。
units.en: Rebels still lived while imperial columns overstayed in the field—both sins on Jing Fang's list.
units.literal: At this time those who had usurped and rebelled under Heaven had not all been executed; armies were for the most part beyond their season.

units.zh: 章帝章和二年夏，旱。
units.en: Drought gripped the summer of Zhanghe 2 under Emperor Zhang.
units.literal: In Zhangdi's second year of Zhanghe, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 時，章帝崩后，竇太后兄弟用事奢僭。
units.en: Emperor Zhang had just died; the Dou brothers flaunted power for their sister the dowager, spending wildly beyond their station.
units.literal: At that time, after Zhangdi died, Empress Dowager Dou's brothers held power, extravagant and usurping.

units.zh: 和帝永元六年秋，京都旱。
units.en: Luoyang baked under drought in the autumn of Yongyuan 6.
units.literal: In Emperor He's sixth year of Yongyuan, autumn, the capital region had drought.

units.zh: 時，雒陽有冤囚，和帝幸雒陽寺，錄囚徒，理冤囚，收令下獄抵罪。
units.en: A miscarriage of justice in Luoyang brought Emperor He in person to the city jail; he freed the innocent, jailed the magistrate, and laid the charge at his door.
units.literal: At that time in Luoyang there were unjust prisoners; He visited the Luoyang jail, reviewed convicts, set right unjust prisoners, seized the magistrate and sent him down to prison to answer for his crime.

units.zh: 行未還宫，澍雨降。
units.en: He had not yet reached the palace when a soaking rain began to fall.
units.literal: Before he had returned walking to the palace, soaking rain fell.

units.zh: 古今注曰：「永元二年，郡國十四旱。十五年，雒陽郡國二十二並旱，或傷稼。」
units.en: The Ancient and Modern Notes add: "Yongyuan 2 brought drought to fourteen provinces; in year 15 twenty-two jurisdictions around Luoyang dried out, ruining crops in places."
units.literal: Ancient and Modern Notes say: "In the second year of Yongyuan, fourteen commanderies and kingdoms had drought. In the fifteenth year, twenty-two commanderies and kingdoms around Luoyang all had drought, in some cases harming the crops."

units.zh: 安帝古今注曰：「永初元年，郡國八旱，分遣議郎請雨。」
units.en: Notes on Emperor An record: "In Yongchu 1 eight provinces droughted; the court sent consultants to pray for rain."
units.literal: The Ancient and Modern Notes for Emperor An say: "In the first year of Yongchu, eight commanderies and kingdoms had drought; gentleman consultants were separately dispatched to pray for rain."

units.zh: 案本紀二年五月，旱，皇太后幸雒陽寺，錄囚徒，即日降雨。
units.en: The annals add: in the fifth month of year 2 drought struck; the empress dowager reviewed Luoyang prisoners and rain came the same day.
units.literal: Examining the Basic Annals: in the fifth month of the second year there was drought; the empress dowager visited the Luoyang jail, reviewed convicts, and rain fell that day.

units.zh: 六月，京都及郡國四十大水。
units.en: In the sixth month forty provinces and the capital flooded.
units.literal: In the sixth month the capital region and forty commanderies and kingdoms had great flood.

units.zh: 雖去旱得水，無救為災。
units.en: Relief from drought brought no rescue—only new disaster.
units.literal: Although drought departed and water came, it could not save them from disaster.

units.zh: 安帝永初六年夏，旱。
units.en: The summer of Yongchu 6 brought drought under Emperor An.
units.literal: In Emperor An's sixth year of Yongchu, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 古今注曰：「三年，郡國八，四年、五年夏，並旱。」
units.en: The notes add: "Drought struck eight provinces in year 3 and returned in the summers of years 4 and 5."
units.literal: Ancient and Modern Notes say: "In the third year eight commanderies and kingdoms; in the fourth and fifth years, summer, all had drought."

units.zh: 七年夏，旱。
units.en: Drought returned the following summer.
units.literal: In the seventh year, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 元初元年夏，旱。
units.en: Yuanchu's first summer was rainless.
units.literal: In the first year of Yuanchu, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 二年夏，旱。
units.en: The next summer brought drought again.
units.literal: In the second year, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 三年夏旱，時西羌寇亂，軍屯相繼，連十餘年。
units.en: In the summer of the third year there was drought; at the time the western Qiang were raiding in rebellion, and garrisons followed one after another for more than ten years.
units.literal: In the summer of the third year there was drought; at the time the western Qiang were raiding in rebellion, and garrisons followed one after another for more than ten years.

units.zh: 六年夏，旱。
units.en: In the sixth year, summer, there was drought.
units.literal: In the sixth year, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 順帝永建三年夏，旱。
units.en: Emperor Shun's third Yongjian summer was a season of drought.
units.literal: In Emperor Shun's third year of Yongjian, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 五年夏，旱。
units.en: Two years later drought struck again.
units.literal: In the fifth year, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 陽嘉二年夏，旱。
units.en: Yangjia 2 brought another rainless summer.
units.literal: In the second year of Yangjia, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 時，李固对策，以爲奢僭所致也。
units.en: Li Gu, answering the court's policy questions, blamed the skies on luxury and overreaching.
units.literal: At that time Li Gu in his examination answer considered that it was caused by extravagance and usurpation.

units.zh: 冲帝永熹元年夏，旱。
units.en: The child-emperor Chong's sole summer reign year opened with drought.
units.literal: In Emperor Chong's first year of Yongxi, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 時，冲帝幼崩，太尉李固勸太后兄梁冀立嗣帝，擇年長有德者，天下賴之，則功名不朽。
units.en: When the boy emperor died, Grand Commandant Li Gu urged the empress dowager's brother Liang Ji to establish an heir-emperor, choosing one advanced in years and possessed of virtue, so that if all under Heaven relied on him their merit and fame would not perish.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Chong died young; Grand Commandant Li Gu urged the empress dowager's brother Liang Ji to establish an heir-emperor, choosing one advanced in years and possessed of virtue; if all under Heaven relied on him, then merit and fame would not perish.

units.zh: 年幼未可知，如后不善，悔无所及。
units.en: A child on the throne is a gamble—if he turns vicious, remorse will come too late.
units.literal: If young, one cannot know; if afterward he is not good, regret will have no reach.

units.zh: 時太后及冀貪立年幼，欲久自傳，遂立質帝，八岁。
units.en: The dowager and Liang Ji preferred a malleable child so they could prolong their regency, and enthroned the eight-year-old Emperor Zhi.
units.literal: At that time the empress dowager and Ji greedily established one who was young, wishing to prolong their own transmission; thereupon they set up Emperor Zhi, eight years old.

units.zh: 此不用德。
units.en: They spurned the counsel of virtue.
units.literal: This was not using virtue.

units.zh: 桓帝元嘉元年夏，旱。
units.en: Emperor Huan's first Yuanjia summer was dry.
units.literal: In Huandi's first year of Yuanjia, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 是時，梁冀秉政，妻、子並受封，寵逾節。
units.en: Liang Ji dominated the court while his wife and sons piled up titles beyond all decency.
units.literal: At that time Liang Ji held power; wife and sons together received enfeoffment; favor exceeded measure.

units.zh: 延熹元年六月，旱。
units.en: The sixth month of Yanxi 1 saw drought.
units.literal: In the first year of Yanxi, sixth month, there was drought.

units.zh: 靈帝熹平五年夏，旱。
units.en: Emperor Ling's fifth Xiping summer brought drought.
units.literal: In Lingdi's fifth year of Xiping, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 蔡邕作伯夷叔齊碑曰「熹平五年，天下大旱，禱請名山，求獲荅應。
units.en: Cai Yong's Stele for Boyi and Shuqi records: "In Xiping 5 the realm suffered drought; the court prayed at sacred peaks for an answer.
units.literal: Cai Yong composed the Stele for Boyi and Shuqi, saying: "In the fifth year of Xiping all under Heaven had great drought; prayers were offered at famous mountains seeking a received response.

units.zh: 時處士平陽蘇騰，字玄成，夢陟首陽，有神馬之使在道。
units.en: The recluse Su Teng of Pingyang, styled Xuancheng, dreamed of climbing Mount Shouyang and met a spirit horse on the path.
units.literal: At that time the retired gentleman Su Teng of Pingyang, courtesy name Xuancheng, dreamed he climbed Mount Shouyang; on the road there was a divine horse envoy.

units.zh: 明覺而思之，以其夢陟狀上聞。
units.en: At dawn he reported the dream to the throne.
units.literal: Awake at dawn he pondered it and reported the form of his dream ascent to the court.

units.zh: 天子開三府請雨使者，與郡縣戶曹掾吏登山升祠。
units.en: The emperor sent rain envoys from the Three Offices with local clerks to climb the mountain and offer sacrifice.
units.literal: The Son of Heaven opened the Three Offices' rain-prayer envoys, who with county and commandery household clerks climbed the mountain and ascended the shrine.

units.zh: 手書要曰：『君況我聖主以洪澤之福。』
units.en: He wrote by hand: 'Lord, bless our sage emperor with abundant rain.'
units.literal: He wrote in his own hand a prayer saying: 'Lord, regard my sage sovereign with the blessing of vast moisture.'

units.zh: 天尋興雲，即降甘雨」也。
units.en: Clouds gathered and sweet rain fell."
units.literal: Heaven soon raised clouds and at once sent sweet rain."

units.zh: 六年夏，旱。
units.en: The following summer was dry as well.
units.literal: In the sixth year, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 光和五年夏，旱。
units.en: Guanghe 5 opened with a drought summer.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Guanghe, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 六年夏，旱。
units.en: The next year the same scourge returned.
units.literal: In the sixth year, summer, there was drought.

units.zh: 是時，常侍、黄門僭作威福。
units.en: Palace eunuchs were then playing tyrant, handing down fortune and ruin at whim.
units.literal: At that time regular attendants and yellow-gate eunuchs usurped making awesomeness and blessings.

units.zh: 獻帝興平元年秋，長安旱。
units.en: Chang'an withered in the autumn of Xingping 1 under Emperor Xian.
units.literal: In Xiandi's first year of Xingping, autumn, Chang'an had drought.

units.zh: 是時，李傕、郭汜專權縱事。
units.en: Li Jue and Guo Si then ran the capital as they pleased.
units.literal: At that time Li Jue and Guo Si monopolized power and gave free rein to affairs.

units.zh: 更始時，南陽有童謠曰：「諧不諧，在赤眉。
units.en: During the Gengshi interregnum a rhyme ran through Nanyang: "Whether the tune holds—ask the Red Eyebrows.
units.literal: In Gengshi's time, Nanyang had a children's song saying: "Harmonious or not harmonious, lies with the Red Eyebrows.

units.zh: 得不得，在河北。」
units.en: Whether the prize is won—look to the north of the Yellow River."
units.literal: Obtaining or not obtaining, lies with Hebei."

units.zh: 是時，更始在長安，世祖爲大司馬平定河北。
units.en: Gengshi held Chang'an while Liu Xiu, as grand marshal, was pacifying the north.
units.literal: At this time Gengshi was in Chang'an; Shizu was grand marshal pacifying Hebei.

units.zh: 更始大臣並僭專權，故謠妖作也。
units.en: Gengshi's ministers had all seized power beyond their right—hence these portentous rhymes.
units.literal: Gengshi's great ministers together usurped sole power; therefore song prodigies arose.

units.zh: 后更始遂爲赤眉所殺，是更始之不諧在赤眉也。
units.en: The Red Eyebrows soon killed Gengshi—the "lack of harmony" line had pointed straight at them.
units.literal: Later Gengshi was then killed by the Red Eyebrows; this was Gengshi's lack of harmony lying with the Red Eyebrows.

units.zh: 世祖自河北興。
units.en: Liu Xiu rose to power from the Hebei plain.
units.literal: Shizu rose from Hebei.

units.zh: 世祖建武六年，蜀童謠曰：「黄牛白腹，五铢當復。」
units.en: In Jianwu 6 a Shu children's rhyme ran: "The yellow bull shows a white belly—the Han five-zhu coin will return."
units.literal: In Shizu's sixth year of Jianwu, Shu had a children's song saying: "Yellow ox, white belly; the five-zhu coin ought to return."

units.zh: 是時，公孙述僭號於蜀，時人窃言王莽称黄，述欲继之，故称白；
units.en: Gongsun Shu had declared himself emperor in Shu; gossips said Wang Mang's regime had been the "yellow" phase and Shu styled itself "white" as his successor;
units.literal: At this time Gongsun Shu usurped title in Shu; people of the time secretly said Wang Mang was called yellow, Shu wished to succeed him, therefore called white;

units.zh: 五铢，漢家货，明當復也。
units.en: the five-zhu was Han coinage—plainly it would be restored.
units.literal: the five-zhu is Han house currency; clearly it ought to return.

units.zh: 述遂誅滅。
units.en: Gongsun Shu was destroyed.
units.literal: He was then executed and destroyed.

units.zh: 王莽末，天水童謠曰：「出吳門，望缇羣。
units.en: Near Wang Mang's fall Tianshui children sang: "Out through Wu Gate, eyes on the Ti hills.
units.literal: At the end of Wang Mang, Tianshui had a children's song saying: "Go out the Wu Gate, gaze at the Ti herd.

units.zh: 見一蹇人，言欲上天；
units.en: There walks a cripple who swears he will climb to Heaven;
units.literal: Seeing one lame man, he says he wishes to ascend Heaven;

units.zh: 令天可上，地上安得民！」
units.en: If Heaven were truly within reach, what people would be left on earth!"
units.literal: supposing Heaven could be ascended, how could there be people on earth!"

units.zh: 時，隗嚣初起兵於天水，后意稍廣，欲爲天子，遂破滅，嚣少病蹇。
units.en: Wei Xiao had launched his rebellion from Tianshui, then dreamed of the throne—and fell; he had been lame from youth, matching the rhyme's cripple.
units.literal: At that time Wei Xiao first raised troops in Tianshui; later his intent gradually broadened, he wished to be Son of Heaven, thereupon was destroyed and perished; Xiao in youth had been ill with lameness.

units.zh: 吳門，冀郭門名也。
units.en: "Wu Gate" was a gate in the Ji capital's wall.
units.literal: Wu Gate is the name of a Ji city gate.

units.zh: 缇羣，山名也。
units.en: "Ti herd" denoted a mountain.
units.literal: Ti herd is a mountain name.

units.zh: 順帝之末，京都童謠曰：「直如弦，死道邊。
units.en: Late in Emperor Shun's reign Luoyang children chanted: "Straight as a bowstring—you end dead in the ditch.
units.literal: At the end of Shundi, the capital had a children's song saying: "Straight as a bowstring—dead beside the road.

units.zh: 曲如鈎，反封侯。」
units.en: Crooked as a fishhook—you win a marquisate instead."
units.literal: Curved like a hook—on the contrary enfeoffed marquis."

units.zh: 案順帝即世，孝質短祚，大將軍梁冀貪树疏幼，以爲己功，專國號令，以赡其私。
units.en: Emperor Shun died; Emperor Zhi reigned briefly; Liang Ji the general-in-chief forced a distant child onto the throne, claimed the credit, and bent every edict to private gain.
units.literal: Examining: when Shundi passed from the world, Xiaozhi had a short reign; the great general Liang Ji greedily set up a distant youth, taking it as his own merit, monopolized state commands, so as to enrich his private interests.

units.zh: 太尉李固以爲清河王雅性聪明，敦詩悦禮，加又属亲，立長則順，置善則固。
units.en: Li Gu urged enthroning the Prince of Qinghe—a clever, cultivated kinsman; the elder line would satisfy the realm, a worthy choice would steady the state.
units.literal: Grand Commandant Li Gu considered that the Prince of Qinghe by nature was intelligent, earnest in the Odes and pleased with the Rites, moreover was of kin by category; establishing the elder then is compliant, setting the good then is firm.

units.zh: 而冀建白太后，策免固，征蠡吾侯，遂即至尊。
units.en: Liang Ji overruled him, secured the dowager's edict, cashiered Li Gu, and brought in the Marquis of Liwu—the future Emperor Huan.
units.literal: But Ji memorialized the empress dowager, ordered dismissal of Gu, summoned the marquis of Liwu, thereupon he ascended the supreme seat.

units.zh: 固是日幽毙於獄，暴尸道路，而太尉胡廣封安樂乡侯、司徒趙戒厨亭侯、司空袁湯安國亭侯云。
units.en: Li Gu died the same day in a dungeon, his body flung in the street, while Hu Guang, Zhao Jie, and Yuan Tang—the ministers who bent to Liang Ji—each walked away with a new noble title.
units.literal: Gu that day was secretly killed in prison, his corpse exposed on the road, while Grand Commandant Hu Guang was enfeoffed marquis of Anle township, Minister of Education Zhao Jie marquis of Chuting pavilion, Minister of Works Yuan Tang marquis of Anguo pavilion, and so on.

units.zh: 桓帝之初，天下童謠曰：「小麦青青大麦枯，誰當獲者婦與姑。
units.en: Early in Emperor Huan's reign a rhyme swept the empire: "Green wheat, blasted barley—who gathers the harvest? Wives and mothers-in-law.
units.literal: At the beginning of Huandi, all under Heaven had a children's song saying: "The wheat is green-green, the barley withered; who shall reap—women and mothers-in-law.

units.zh: 丈人何在西击胡，吏買馬，君具車，請爲諸君鼓咙胡。」
units.en: Where are the men? Off west fighting the Hu; clerks must buy horses, masters fit the carts—let me hum a marching tune for you all."
units.literal: Why is the old man in the west striking the Hu; clerks buy horses, you prepare the carts; I beg to for you all beat the throat Hu."

units.zh: 案元嘉中凉州諸羌一時俱反，南入蜀、漢，東抄三輔，延及並、冀，大爲民害。
units.en: In the Yuanjia years the Liangzhou Qiang revolted as one, poured into Ba and Han, pillaged the capital region, and spread ruin through Bing and Ji.
units.literal: Examining: in the Yuanjia period the various Qiang of Liangzhou together at one time all rebelled, entered south into Shu and Han, raided east the Three Adjuncts, extended to Bing and Ji, greatly becoming harm to the people.

units.zh: 命將出眾，每戰常负，中國益发甲卒，麦多委棄，但有婦女獲刈之也。
units.en: Imperial armies marched and lost again and again; conscripts multiplied while grain rotted in the fields—only women were left to scythe what they could.
units.literal: Ordered generals went out with hosts; in each battle they constantly lost; the central states ever more sent armored soldiers; much wheat was cast aside and abandoned; only there were women who reaped and cut it.

units.zh: 吏買馬，君具車者，言调发重及有秩者也。
units.en: The line about clerks, horses, and masters' carts meant crushing levies on every salaried official.
units.literal: "Clerks buy horses, you prepare carts" means speaking of heavy levies reaching those with rank.

units.zh: 請爲諸君鼓咙胡者，不敢公言，私咽語。
units.en: "Let me hum for you" meant the people dared not speak aloud and muttered their grievances in their throats.
units.literal: "I beg to for you all beat the throat Hu" means not daring to speak openly, privately swallowing words.

units.zh: 桓帝之初，京都童謠曰：「城上烏，尾畢逋，公爲吏，子爲徒。
units.en: Another Luoyang rhyme in Emperor Huan's early years ran: "Crows on the city wall, tails all frayed—fathers turned clerks, sons turned convicts.
units.literal: At the beginning of Huandi, the capital had a children's song saying: "The crow on the wall, tail all scattered; the father is clerk, the son is convict laborer.

units.zh: 一徒死，百乘車。
units.en: One conscript dies—a hundred carriages roll.
units.literal: One convict laborer dies, a hundred carriages.

units.zh: 車班班，入河間。
units.en: Carriages in long lines—winding their way to Hejian.
units.literal: Carriages in rows, enter Hejian.

units.zh: 河間姹女工數錢，以錢爲室金爲堂。
units.en: The Hejian belle counts her coins—rooms built of copper cash, halls sheeted in gold.
units.literal: The Hejian beauty is skilled at counting cash; she takes cash for chamber and gold for hall.

units.zh: 石上慊慊舂黄粱。
units.en: On the stone mortar, pestles thump—only yellow millet left to grind.
units.literal: On the stone, sorrowfully pounding yellow millet.

units.zh: 梁下有悬鼓，我欲击之丞卿怒。」
units.en: A line from the rhyme: "There's a petition drum under the rafters—I reach for the mallet, but the chancellor and his men fly into a rage."
units.literal: Beneath the beam hangs a drum; I wish to strike it, but the assistant minister and chief ministers grow angry."

units.zh: 案此皆謂爲政貪也。
units.en: The commentary takes every image in that song as a verdict on rapacious rule.
units.literal: Examining: all these are said to mean grasping greed in government.

units.zh: 城上烏，尾畢逋者，處高利独食，不與下共，謂人主多聚敛也。
units.en: The rooftop crow hoarding scraps alone foretells a Son of Heaven who squeezes the realm for revenue and shares nothing downward.
units.literal: "The crow on the wall, tail all scattered" means occupying high profit and eating alone, not sharing with those below; it speaks of the ruler greatly amassing revenue.

units.zh: 公爲吏，子爲徒者，言蛮夷將叛逆，父既爲軍吏，其子又爲卒徒往击之也。
units.en: Fathers pressed into the army clerks' corps and sons dragooned as convict troops point to frontier revolts that devour one generation after another.
units.literal: "The father is clerk, the son convict laborer" means the barbarians will rebel; the father having already been a military clerk, his son again becomes foot-soldier and convict laborer to go strike them.

units.zh: 一徒死，百乘車者，言前一人往討胡既死矣，后又遣百乘車往。
units.en: One expeditionary column perishes; the court answers by flinging a hundred more chariots into the same meat grinder.
units.literal: "One convict laborer dies, a hundred carriages" means the first man sent to punish the Hu already died, afterward again a hundred carriages were dispatched.

units.zh: 車班班，入河間者，言上將崩，乘舆班班入河間迎靈帝也。
units.en: The long train rolling toward Hejian foretold the emperor's death and the hearse-road that would bring Emperor Ling from Hejian to the throne.
units.literal: "Carriages in rows, enter Hejian" means the sovereign is about to die; imperial carriages in rows enter Hejian to welcome Emperor Ling.

units.zh: 應劭釋此句云：「徵靈帝者，輪班擁節入河閒也。」
units.en: Ying Shao glossed the line: "Calling for Emperor Ling means imperial escorts winding into Hejian in long columns."
units.literal: Ying Shao explains this line: "Summoning Emperor Ling means carriages in rows bearing credentials enter Hejian."

units.zh: 河間姹女工數錢，一本作「妖女」。
units.en: The Hejian belle counting coins—one manuscript reads 'bewitching woman' instead.
units.literal: The Hejian beauty skilled at counting cash—in one text reads 'bewitching woman.'

units.zh: 以錢爲室金爲堂者，靈帝既立，其母永樂太后好聚金以爲堂也。
units.en: Coins for rooms and gold for halls pictured Empress Dowager Yongle hoarding metal to gild her halls once her son took the throne.
units.literal: "Taking cash for chamber and gold for hall" means after Ling was enthroned, his mother Empress Dowager Yongle loved amassing gold to build halls.

units.zh: 石上慊慊舂黄粱者，言永樂雖积金錢，慊慊常苦不足，使人舂黄粱而食之也。
units.en: The pestle on the mortar meant that even mountains of gold could not sate her—she still grudged every grain and made servants pound millet as if famine stalked the harem.
units.literal: "Sorrowfully pounding yellow millet on the stone" means although Yongle piled gold and cash, she sorrowfully always suffered insufficiency, and had people pound yellow millet and eat it.

units.zh: 梁下有悬鼓，我欲击之丞卿怒者，言永樂主教靈帝，使卖官受錢，所祿非其人，天下忠笃之士怨望，欲击悬鼓以求見，丞卿主鼓者，亦復谄順，怒而止我也。
units.en: The blocked drumbeat pictured honest men who wished to pound the grievance drum only to find the Yongle faction—having taught the emperor to vend offices—had bribed every gatekeeper; the very officials who should relay petitions silenced them instead.
units.literal: "Beneath the beam hangs a drum; I wish to strike it, but the assistant minister and chief ministers grow angry" means Yongle instructed Ling to sell offices and receive money, so that salaries went to unworthy men; loyal and sincere knights of the realm resented and wished to strike the hanging drum to seek audience; the assistant and minister in charge of the drum likewise flattered and yielded and angrily stopped them.

units.zh: 桓帝之初，京都童謠曰：「游平卖印自有平，不辟豪賢及大姓。」
units.en: Another capital rhyme at the start of Emperor Huan's reign ran: "You Ping vends the seals—and balance returns; he shows no favor to magnates or great houses."
units.literal: At the beginning of Huandi, the capital had a children's song saying: "You Ping sells seals and there is peace; it does not avoid powerful worthies and great clans."

units.zh: 案到延熹之末，鄧皇后以譴自殺，乃以竇貴人代之，其父名武字游平，拜城門校尉。
units.en: By late Yanxi Empress Deng had been forced to suicide; Honored Lady Dou replaced her. Her father Dou Wu, whose courtesy name was You Ping, became colonel of the city gates—the very "You Ping" of the rhyme.
units.literal: Examining: when it reached the end of Yanxi, Empress Deng by reproach committed suicide, then the Honored Lady Dou was substituted; her father was named Wu, style You Ping, and was appointed colonel of the city gates.

units.zh: 及太后攝政，爲大將軍，與太傅陳蕃合心戮力，惟德是建，印綬所加，咸得其人，豪賢大姓，皆絕望矣。
units.en: Under the regency Dou Wu served as general-in-chief beside Grand Tutor Chen Fan; together they handed offices only to worthy men, slamming the door on every great clan that had bought favor under the Liangs.
units.literal: When the empress dowager held the regency, he became great general; with grand tutor Chen Fan he united hearts and joined strength; only virtue was established; wherever seals and ribbons were bestowed, all obtained the right men; powerful worthies and great clans were all cut off from hope.

units.zh: 桓帝之末，京都童謠曰：「茅田一頃中有井，四方纤纤不可整。
units.en: Late in Emperor Huan's reign Luoyang sang: "A hempfield of one qing with a well at its heart—ragged on every side, beyond all mending.
units.literal: At the end of Huandi, the capital had a children's song saying: "A thatched field of one qing has a well in it; on four sides, fine and fine, it cannot be set straight.

units.zh: 嚼復嚼，今年尚可后年鐃。」
units.en: Chew and chew—this year we scrape by; next year they'll beat the warning bells."
units.literal: Chew again, chew again; this year is still tolerable, next year the nao bells."

units.zh: 案《易》曰：「拔茅茹以其汇，征吉。」
units.en: The Classic of Changes counsels: "Uproot the reed and its runners together—then the campaign is lucky."
units.literal: Examining the Changes, it says: "Pull up the rush by its roots, with its kind; the expedition is auspicious."

units.zh: 茅喻羣賢也。
units.en: Here the reed patch stands for the cluster of honest ministers.
units.literal: Rush stands for the host of worthies.

units.zh: 井者，法也。
units.en: The well in the field is the standard of law still holding at the center.
units.literal: The well means law.

units.zh: 於時中常侍管霸、苏康憎疾海内英哲，與長樂少府劉嚣、太常許咏、尚書柳分、袁山松書曰，柳分權豪之黨，為范滂所奏者。
units.en: Regular palace attendants Guan Ba and Su Kang loathed outstanding worthies of the realm; with the junior privy treasurer of Changle Liu Ao, the chamberlain for ceremonies Xu Yong, and the imperial secretary Liu Fen they formed a clique; Yuan Shansong's Book notes that Liu Fen belonged to the power-broker faction impeached by Fan Pang.
units.literal: At that time regular palace attendants Guan Ba and Su Kang hated outstanding worthies of the realm; with junior privy treasurer of Changle Liu Ao, chamberlain for ceremonies Xu Yong, and secretariat director Liu Fen—Yuan Shansong's Book says Liu Fen was of the powerful magnates' faction, impeached by Fan Pang.

units.zh: 尋穆、史佟、佟後亦為司隸。
units.en: Xun Mu and Shi Tong joined them; Tong later became metropolitan commandant.
units.literal: Xun Mu and Shi Tong—Tong later also became metropolitan commandant.

units.zh: 應劭曰，史佟，左官媮進者也。
units.en: Ying Shao calls Shi Tong a minor officer who schemed his way upward.
units.literal: Ying Shao says Shi Tong was a petty official who stole advancement.

units.zh: 司隸唐珍等，代作脣齒。
units.en: Metropolitan Commandant Tang Zhen and the rest covered one another like lip and teeth.
