units.literal: Metropolitan commandant Tang Zhen and others substituted for one another as lips and teeth.

units.zh: 河内牢川詣闕上書：「汝、颍、南陽，上采虚誉，專作威福；
units.en: A certain Lao Chuan of Henei petitioned the throne: "Runan, Yingchuan, and Nanyang traffic in hollow fame and throw their weight about unchecked;
units.literal: A man of Henei, Lao Chuan, went to the palace gate and submitted a memorial: "Runan, Yingchuan, and Nanyang upward gather empty reputation and exclusively make awesomeness and blessings;

units.zh: 甘陵有南北二部，三輔尤甚。」
units.en: Ganling is split into rival southern and northern cliques, and the capital region is worse still."
units.literal: Ganling has south and north factions; the Three Adjuncts are still worse."

units.zh: 由是傳考黄門北寺，始見廢閣。
units.en: The case was kicked to the eunuchs' North Prison; for the first time the full machinery of purge and prison came into view.
units.literal: Thereupon they transmitted for examination the Northern Office of the Yellow Gates, and for the first time saw dismissal and closure.

units.zh: 茅田一頃者，言羣賢眾多也。
units.en: The wide hempfield meant many good men still stood in court.
units.literal: "A thatched field of one qing" means the host of worthies is numerous.

units.zh: 中有井者，言雖厄窮，不失其法度也。
units.en: The well promised that even in distress the rule of law would not be lost.
units.literal: "Having a well in it" means although in straits, one does not lose one's measure of law.

units.zh: 四方纤纤不可整者，言姦慝大炽，不可整理。
units.en: The frayed edges meant villainy had flared beyond correction.
units.literal: "On four sides, fine and fine, it cannot be set straight" means treacherous wickedness blazes greatly and cannot be ordered.

units.zh: 嚼復嚼者，京都飲酒相強之辞也。
units.en: "Chew again" echoed the toasts by which Luoyang nobles bullied each other into another cup.
units.literal: "Chew again, chew again" is the capital's phrase for pressing one another to drink.

units.zh: 言食肉者鄙，不恤王政，徒耽宴飲歌呼而已也。
units.en: It mocked meat-eating grandees who ignored the state and drowned only in banquet noise.
units.literal: It means those who eat meat are base; they do not pity royal government, but only indulge in feasting, drinking, and shouting.

units.zh: 今年尚可者，言但禁錮也。
units.en: "This year we scrape by" meant the court still stopped at stripping offices—mere faction proscription.
units.literal: "This year is still tolerable" means only proscription.

units.zh: 后年鐃者，陳、竇被誅，天下大壞。
units.en: "Next year the bells" was the massacre of Chen Fan and Dou Wu and the collapse that followed.
units.literal: "Next year the nao bells" means Chen and Dou were executed and all under Heaven was greatly ruined.

units.zh: 桓帝之末，京都童謠曰：「白盖小車何延延。
units.en: Another late-Huan rhyme went: "Little white-topped coaches—what an endless stream!
units.literal: At the end of Huandi, the capital had a children's song saying: "Little white-canopied carriages, how they stretch on and on.

units.zh: 河間來合諧，河間來合諧！」
units.en: From Hejian they come, all in tune—from Hejian they come, all in tune!"
units.literal: Hejian comes in harmony; Hejian comes in harmony!"

units.zh: 案解犊亭属饶陽河間县也。
units.en: Jiedu Post stood in Raoyang county under Hejian—ground zero for the omen.
units.literal: Examining: Jiedu Pavilion belongs to Raoyang in Hejian county.

units.zh: 居无幾何而桓帝崩，使者與解犊侯皆白盖車從河間來。
units.en: Within weeks Emperor Huan was dead; heralds and the Marquis of Jiedu rolled toward Luoyang in white-canopied wagons from Hejian.
units.literal: Before long Huandi died; envoys and the marquis of Jiedu both rode white-canopied carts coming from Hejian.

units.zh: 延延，眾貌也。
units.en: Yanyan painted the long, crowded train of coaches.
units.literal: Yanyan is the appearance of a crowd.

units.zh: 是時御史劉儵建議立靈帝，以儵爲侍中，中常侍侯览畏其亲近，必當間己，白拜儵泰山太守，因令司隸迫促殺之。
units.en: Liu You had urged Liu Hong's accession and won a palace post; Hou Lan, fearing a rival at the emperor's ear, had him packed off to Taishan and hounded to death by the metropolitan commandant.
units.literal: At that time imperial secretary Liu You proposed establishing Emperor Ling; he was made palace attendant; palace attendant Hou Lan feared he would be intimate with the sovereign and would surely alienate himself from Lan, and so memorialized to appoint You grand administrator of Taishan, then ordered the Metropolitan Province to press and hurry and kill him.

units.zh: 朝廷少長，思其功效，乃拔用其弟郃，致位司徒，此爲合諧也。
units.en: Courtiers remembered Liu You's service and raised his brother Liu He to minister of education—Hejian's "harmony" made good after all.
units.literal: The court, young and old, thought of his merit and effect; thereupon they promoted and used his younger brother He, reaching the position of minister of education; this was "coming in harmony."

units.zh: 靈帝之末，京都童謠曰：「侯非侯，王非王，千乘萬騎上北芒。」
units.en: As Emperor Ling's reign failed, children sang: "No lord is lord, no king is king—thousands of chariots climb Beimang Hill."
units.literal: At the end of Lingdi, the capital had a children's song saying: "He is no marquis, the king is no king; a thousand chariots and ten thousand riders ascend Beimang."

units.zh: 案到中平六年，史侯登蹑至尊，獻帝未有爵號，爲中常侍段珪等數十人所執，公卿百官皆随其后，到河上，乃得來還。
units.en: In Zhongping 6 Marquis Shi mounted the supreme seat; Emperor Xian still had no noble title. He was seized by palace attendant Duan Gui and several tens of others; the dukes, ministers, and all officials followed, and only when they reached the river could they return.
units.literal: Examining: when it reached the sixth year of Zhongping, Marquis Shi mounted the supreme seat step by step; Emperor Xian had not yet a noble title; he was seized by several tens of persons including palace attendant Duan Gui; dukes, ministers, and all officials followed behind them; only when they reached the river were they able to return.

units.zh: 此爲非侯非王上北芒者也。
units.en: That was the scene the rhyme called "no marquis, no king, climbing Beimang."
units.literal: This was "not marquis, not king, ascending Beimang."

units.zh: 英雄記曰：「京師謠歌咸言『河臘叢進』，獻帝臘日生也。
units.en: The Record of Heroes notes capital rhymes chanting 'River La, swarm forward'—Emperor Xian was born on a la day.
units.literal: Record of Heroes says: "Capital songs and rhymes all said 'River La, cluster advance'—Emperor Xian was born on the la day.

units.zh: 風俗通曰：『烏臘烏臘。』」
units.en: The Fengsu Tong echoes: 'Crow-la, crow-la.'"
units.literal: Fengsu Tong says: 'Crow-la, crow-la.'"

units.zh: 案逆臣董卓滔天虐民，窮凶極惡，關東舉兵欲共誅之，轉相顧望，莫肯先進，處處停兵數十萬，若烏臘蟲，相隨橫取之矣。
units.en: The rhymes mocked Dong Zhuo: eastern lords mustered vast armies yet hung back like crow-la grubs, plundering in packs instead of striking first.
units.literal: Examining: the rebellious minister Dong Zhuo overwhelmed Heaven and abused the people, utterly vicious; the eastern passes raised armies wishing together to execute him, but looked to one another in turn, none willing to advance first; everywhere armies halted by the hundreds of thousands, like crow-la insects, following one another in seizing by force.

units.zh: 靈帝中平中，京都歌曰：「承樂世董逃，游四郭董逃，蒙天恩董逃，带金紫董逃，行谢恩董逃，整車騎董逃，垂欲发董逃，與中辞董逃，出西門董逃，瞻宫殿董逃，望京城董逃，日夜絕董逃，心摧傷董逃。」
units.en: Mid-Zhongping Luoyang took up a bitter refrain: every line of life's pomp ended in the refrain "Dong flees"—a drumbeat on the name Dong Zhuo.
units.literal: In Lingdi's Zhongping era, the capital had a song saying: "Receiving happy times—Dong flees; roaming the four outer walls—Dong flees; receiving Heaven's grace—Dong flees; wearing gold and purple—Dong flees; walking to thank grace—Dong flees; arraying chariots and horse—Dong flees; about to set out—Dong flees; taking leave in the palace—Dong flees; going out the west gate—Dong flees; gazing at palace halls—Dong flees; looking at the capital city—Dong flees; day and night cut off—Dong flees; heart broken and wounded—Dong flees."

units.zh: 案「董」謂董卓也，言雖跋扈，縱其残暴，終歸逃窜，至於滅族也。
units.en: The hidden word was Dong Zhuo: "however he strutted, the song foretold he would end in flight and clan extinction."
units.literal: Examining: "Dong" means Dong Zhuo; although he was domineering and let loose his cruelty and violence, in the end he fled and scattered until his clan was exterminated.

units.zh: 風俗通曰：「卓以董逃之歌主為己發，大禁絕之，死者千數。」
units.en: The Fengsu Tong notes: "Dong Zhuo read the 'Dong flees' songs as personal attacks, banned them utterly, and killed thousands."
units.literal: Fengsu Tong says: "Zhuo took the refrain of the Dong-flees song as aimed at himself and strictly forbade it; those who died numbered in the thousands."

units.zh: 靈帝之末，禮樂崩壞，賞刑失中，毀譽無驗，競飾偽服，以盪典制，遠近翕然，咸名後生放聲者為時人。
units.en: By Ling's last years ritual and music had collapsed, justice had lost its measure, and youths who shouted the latest rhymes were hailed as "men of the moment" from every quarter.
units.literal: At the end of Emperor Ling, rites and music collapsed; rewards and punishments lost their balance; praise and blame had no verification; people vied in decking false dress to overturn canonical institutions; near and far alike, all called youths who raised their voices "men of the age."

units.zh: 有識者竊言：舊曰世人，次曰俗人，今更曰時人，此天促其期也。
units.en: Thoughtful men whispered: once people were "folk of the realm," then "vulgar men," now "men of the age"—Heaven was shortening the dynasty's span.
units.literal: Men of insight privately said: formerly one said "men of the world," next "vulgar men," now again "men of the age"—this is Heaven shortening the term.

units.zh: 其閒無幾，天下大壞也。
units.en: Within little time the realm was utterly broken.
units.literal: Before long, all under Heaven was greatly ruined.

units.zh: 獻帝践祚之初，京都童謠曰：「千里草，何青青。
units.en: When Emperor Xian first mounted the throne, Luoyang children chanted: "The grass that runs a thousand li—how lush and green!
units.literal: At the beginning of Xiandi's treading the throne, the capital had a children's song saying: "Thousand-mile grass, how green-green.

units.zh: 十日卜，不得生。」
units.en: Ten days atop the divination sign—no survivor below."
units.literal: Ten days divination—cannot obtain life."

units.zh: 案千里草爲董，十日卜爲卓。
units.en: Read as a riddle, the lines stack into the characters for Dong Zhuo.
units.literal: Examining: "thousand-mile grass" makes Dong; "ten days" atop "divination" makes Zhuo.

units.zh: 凡别字之體，皆從上起，左右离合，无有從下发端者也。
units.en: Charade characters normally stack from the top outward; none start from the bottom and climb upward.
units.literal: In general the form of variant-character riddles all begins from the top, left and right joining and separating; there is none that begins from the bottom issuing upward.

units.zh: 今二字如此者，天意若曰：卓自下摩上，以臣陵君也。
units.en: So Heaven arranged the pieces to show Zhuo thrusting upward from below, a subject bullying his sovereign.
units.literal: Now that the two characters are thus, Heaven's intent was as if saying: Zhuo from below rubs upward, using minister to encroach on lord.

units.zh: 青青者，暴盛之貌也。
units.en: "Green-green" pictured his swagger at its height.
units.literal: Green-green is the appearance of violent flourishing.

units.zh: 不得生者，亦旋破亡。
units.en: "No survivor below" meant he would soon be destroyed.
units.literal: "Cannot obtain life" means likewise soon destroyed and perished.

units.zh: 獻帝初童謠曰：「燕南垂，趙北際，中央不合大如礪，唯有此中可避世。」
units.en: Early in Emperor Xian's reign children sang: "Yan's south, Zhao's north—the middle won't close, wide as a whetstone; only here can you flee the world."
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xian a children's song said: "Yan's southern edge, Zhao's northern border, the center does not join—large as a whetstone; only within this may one escape the age."

units.zh: 公孫瓚以為易地當之，遂徙鎮焉，乃修城積穀，以待天下之變。
units.en: Gongsun Zan read it as naming Yidi, moved his headquarters there, fortified the city, stockpiled grain, and waited for empire-wide upheaval.
units.literal: Gongsun Zan took it that Yidi matched the omen; thereupon he moved his command there, repaired walls and amassed grain, waiting for changes in the realm.

units.zh: 建安三年，袁紹攻瓚，瓚大敗，縊其姊妹妻子，引火自焚，紹兵趣登臺斬之。
units.en: In Jian'an 3 Yuan Shao attacked Zan; Zan was greatly defeated, strangled his sisters, wife, and children, set fire and burned himself; Shao's troops rushed up the tower and beheaded him.
units.literal: In the third year of Jian'an Yuan Shao attacked Zan; Zan was greatly defeated, strangled his sisters and wife and children, set fire and burned himself; Shao's troops rushed up the tower and beheaded him.

units.zh: 初，瓚破黃巾，殺劉虞，乘勝南下，侵據齊地。
units.en: Once he had broken the Yellow Turbans and killed Liu Yu, he swept south and seized Qi.
units.literal: At first Zan defeated the Yellow Turbans, killed Liu Yu, rode victory south, and encroached on Qi territory.

units.zh: 雄威大振，而不能開廓遠圖，欲以堅城觀時，坐聽圍戮，斯亦自易地而去世也。
units.en: His fame peaked, but he never looked beyond his walls, waited passively for siege—and perished in the very "Yidi" the rhyme had named.
units.literal: His fierce prestige greatly shook the land, yet he could not open a broad far-reaching plan; wishing to watch the times from a strong city, he sat listening to siege and slaughter—this too was dying by the very Yidi of the omen.

units.zh: 建安初，荆州童謠曰：「八九年間始欲衰，至十三年无孑遺。」
units.en: Early in Jian'an a Jingzhou rhyme warned: "Around the eighth or ninth year the bloom fades; by the thirteenth nothing remains."
units.literal: At the beginning of Jian'an, Jingzhou had a children's song saying: "Between eight and nine years it first begins to decline; by the thirteenth year not a sprig is left."

units.zh: 言自中興以來，荆州无破亂，及劉表爲牧，民又豐樂，至此逮八九年。
units.en: Since the Guangwu restoration Jingzhou had known peace; under Liu Biao the people prospered—for about eight or nine years.
units.literal: It means from the restoration onward Jingzhou had not been broken in disorder, and when Liu Biao became shepherd the people were again abundant and happy; here it reached eight or nine years.

units.zh: 當始衰者，謂劉表妻當死，諸將並零落也。
units.en: "When it first declines" means Liu Biao's wife was about to die, and the various generals would fall away and scatter.
units.literal: "When it first declines" means Liu Biao's wife was about to die, and the various generals together fell away scattered.

units.zh: 十三年无孑遺者，言十三年表又當死，民當移詣冀州也。
units.en: "By the thirteenth year not a sprig is left" means in the thirteenth year Biao too was about to die, and the people were about to move to Ji Province.
units.literal: "By the thirteenth year not a sprig is left" means in the thirteenth year Biao again was about to die, and the people were about to shift to Ji Province.

units.zh: 干竇搜神記曰：「是時華容有女子忽啼呼云：『〔荊州將〕有大喪！』
units.en: Gan Bao's Record of Searching for Spirits tells how in Huarong a woman suddenly shrieked: 'The governor of Jingzhou faces a great death!'
units.literal: Gan Bao's Record of Searching for Spirits says: "At that time in Huarong a woman suddenly wailed and cried: 'The governor of Jingzhou will have a great bereavement!'

units.zh: 言語過差，縣以為妖言，繫獄百餘日，忽於獄中哭曰：『劉荊州今日死。』
units.en: Officials jailed her for seditious talk. Months later she wailed in prison: 'Liu of Jingzhou dies today.'
units.literal: Her speech was excessive; the county took it for demonic talk and imprisoned her for more than a hundred days. Suddenly in prison she wept: 'Governor Liu of Jingzhou dies today.'

units.zh: 華容去州數〔百里〕，即遣馬吏驗視，〔而劉〕表果死。
units.en: Riders sent hundreds of li found Liu Biao dead as she had said.
units.literal: Huarong was several hundred li from the provincial seat; they at once sent a mounted clerk to verify, and Liu Biao indeed died.

units.zh: 縣乃出之。
units.en: The county then freed her.
units.literal: The county then released her.

units.zh: 續又歌吟曰：『不意李立為貴人。』
units.en: She sang again: 'Who would guess Li Li becomes the great man?'
units.literal: Continuing, she sang: 'Unexpected—Li Li becomes an honored man.'

units.zh: 後無幾，曹公平荊州，以涿郡李立，字建賢，為荊州刺史。」
units.en: Soon Cao Cao pacified Jingzhou and made Li Li of Zhuo, styled Jianxian, provincial inspector."
units.literal: Before long Cao Gong pacified Jingzhou and appointed Li Li of Zhuo commandery, courtesy name Jianxian, as inspector of Jingzhou."

units.zh: 順帝陽嘉元年十月中，望都蒲陰狼殺童兒九十七人。
units.en: In the tenth month of Yangjia 1 wolves slaughtered ninety-seven children in Wangdu and Puyin.
units.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yangjia under Shundi, in Wangdu and Puyin wolves killed ninety-seven children.

units.zh: 時，李固对策，引京房《易傳》曰「君將无道，害將及人，去之深山以全身，厥妖狼食人」。
units.en: Li Gu quoted Jing Fang: "When the ruler loses the Way, disaster reaches the people—flee to the hills; Heaven sends wolves to devour them."
units.literal: At that time Li Gu in his examination answer cited Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes: "When the lord is about to be without the Way, harm will reach men; leave for deep mountains to preserve the whole body; its prodigy is wolves devouring people."

units.zh: 陛下覺寤，比求隱滞，故狼災息。
units.en: The emperor took the hint, sought out neglected talent, and the wolf scourge—so the memorial claimed—abated.
units.literal: Your Majesty awoke and compared, seeking the hidden and stuck; therefore wolf disaster ceased.

units.zh: 東觀書曰：「中山相朱遂到官，不出奉祠北嶽。
units.en: The Eastern Pavilion Account records: "When Zhu Su took office as administrator of Zhongshan he never went to worship the Northern Sacred Peak.
units.literal: The Eastern Pavilion Account says: "Zhu Su, administrator of Zhongshan, on reaching office did not go forth to offer sacrifice at Mount Heng.

units.zh: 詔曰：『災暴緣類，符驗不虛，政失厥中，狼災為應，至乃殘食孩幼，朝廷愍悼，思惟咎徵，博訪其故。
units.en: The throne replied: 'Calamities come in kind; omens do not lie. When rule loses its center wolves answer—even devouring children. The court mourns and searches widely for the cause.
units.literal: An edict said: 'Disasters violently follow their kind; tokens and proofs are not empty. Government loses its balance and wolf disasters respond, even to devouring infants. The court grieves and reflects on blame-omens, broadly seeking the cause.

units.zh: 山嶽尊靈，國所望秩，而遂比不奉祠，怠慢廢典，不務懇惻，淫刑放濫，害加孕婦，毒流未生，感和致災。
units.en: Sacred peaks sustain the state's rites, yet Su neglected them, abandoned the canon, indulged cruel punishments, harmed pregnant women, and poisoned the unborn—drawing disaster by his neglect.
units.literal: Mountains and peaks are honored spirits on whom the state relies for rank, yet Su repeatedly did not offer sacrifice—neglecting and abandoning the canon, not devoting himself to earnest care, letting licentious punishments run wild, harming pregnant women, poison flowing to the unborn, feeling and summoning disaster.

units.zh: 其詳思改救，追復所失。
units.en: He must reform thoroughly and recover what was lost.
units.literal: Let him carefully consider reform and rescue, recovering what was lost.

units.zh: 有不遵憲，舉正以聞。』」
units.en: Whoever violates the law, report him for punishment.'"
units.literal: If any do not obey the statutes, report them for correction.'"

units.zh: 靈帝建寧中，羣狼數十頭入晉陽南城門嚙人。
units.en: During Jianning a pack of wolves burst through Jinyang's south gate and mauled townsfolk.
units.literal: In Lingdi's Jianning era, a pack of several tens of wolves entered the south gate of Jinyang and bit people.
